title: Hero 'Taxes & deductions' chip shows the uncapped total, so it disagrees with the Breakdown and with Gross − Take-home whenever flat deductions exceed gross

title: A blanked or garbage multiplier differential is coerced to 0×, silently pricing every shift of that type at $0
where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:1046-1047 (sanitizeData: `amount: isFinite(amt) ? amt : 0` regardless of type); 4715 (Settings multiplier NumInput with min={0}); 4016-4023 (NumInput commits `min` on an empty field); 1121 (hourlyRate: `base * diff.amount`)
detail: For a dollar-type differential, 0 is the neutral value. Two paths produce it: NumInput's blank→min contract commits 0 when the user clears the '×' field and blurs, and sanitizeData maps any non-finite blob value to 0 rather than to 1. Once written, 0 is a finite number so sanitizeData keeps it on every subsequent load; nothing ever repairs it.
failure: In Settings, tap the Holiday '1.5 ×' field, select-all/delete to retype, then tap elsewhere before typing (common on a phone). Holiday becomes 0×. Add a probe: sanitizeData({differentials:{holiday:{type:'multiplier',amount:''}}}).differentials.holiday.amount === 1 and hourlyRate(50,{type:'multiplier',amount:0}) is never reached from a sanitized blob.

title: Independently rounded chips: Gross − Taxes ≠ Take-home by $1 in ~11% of pay periods; Breakdown rows drift the same way
where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:3484-3487 (hero: fmt(calc.net), fmt(calc.gross), fmt(calc.ded) each rounded separately); 3982-3987 and 4006 (Breakdown: six rows and the take-home each rounded separately); fmt at 1116
detail: `fmt` rounds each figure to whole dollars on its own, so the three hero chips are three independent roundings of gross, ded and gross−ded. Replaying the real shiftGross/computeNet formulas over 220 mixes of base/night 12h shifts at five base rates with default taxes, 24 (11%) print chips whose subtraction is off by one. With six Breakdown rows the residual can reach $3. This is the 'rounding that compounds' the lens asks about — small, but it is the arithmetic a nurse is most likely to check by hand, and the app's credibility rests on the numbers closing.
failure: Two 12h base shifts at the default $65.15/hr, default taxes: hero prints 'Gross $1,564 · Taxes & deductions –$346' over a take-home of '$1,217'. 1,564 − 346 = 1,218.
fix: Display-only: derive the chip as `Math.round(calc.gross) - Math.round(calc.net)` (and likewise give Breakdown the rounding residual on its largest row, or print cents), so the visible figures always close. No change to net/gross/ded themselves — but it changes displayed dollar text, so run the wage-core equality assertion and name this as the one intended difference.
dissent:
The mechanism is real and I reproduced the exact numbers: computeNet(1563.6, defaultTaxes) with two 12h base shifts at $65.15/hr gives gross=1563.6, ded=346.3374, net=1217.2626. fmt() independently rounds each to fmt(gross)=$1,564, fmt(ded)=$346, fmt(net)=$1,217, and indeed 1564−346=1218≠1217 as displayed. So the arithmetic claim checks out exactly.

But granting the mechanism doesn't make the described outcome a bug worth reporting. Critically, computeNet (index.html:1231-1250) computes net = gross - ded in full floating-point precision from the raw, unrounded gross and ded — it is not derived by subtracting two already-rounded whole-dollar numbers. So the underlying wage math (Invariant 3's domain: shiftGross/hourlyRate/computeNet) is exact and internally consistent; nothing compounds or drifts in the actual computation. What the finding calls a defect is that fmt() — used identically everywhere in this codebase (hero chips, Breakdown rows, YearList, etc.) — rounds each of several related, independently-meaningful currency figures to the nearest whole dollar for *display* only. That a rounded subtotal minus a rounded deduction can differ by $1 from the rounded total is an unavoidable, universal property of showing whole-dollar rounded figures for numbers that don't happen to round the same way (the same artifact appears on bank statements, invoices, and virtually every budgeting app that shows subtotal/tax/total as separately rounded whole-currency amounts). Nothing in CLAUDE.md, the wage-core invariant, or the smoke-test suite promises penny-exact (or dollar-exact) reconciliation between independently displayed chips — that's a bar the finding invents and then holds the code to. The claimed severity ("the app's credibility rests on the numbers closing") is a rhetorical overstatement of a $1 cosmetic rounding artifact in a whole-dollar display, not a wage-math correctness bug, and doesn't rise to something the owner needs to act on.

title: Pattern lab and calendar price a toggled-off differential differently
where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:1206-1213 (patternCellShiftType resolves a 'night'/weekend cell to 'base' unless differentials[k].active); 2646 (statOf) and 2795 (calc) call shiftGross(baseRate, differentials[s.shiftType], s) with no active check; hourlyRate 1119-1124
detail: The Settings toggle dims the row and removes the chip from the Add-Shift sheet (4099), and the lab treats it as 'she doesn't get this differential' — but calc/statOf/yearMonths keep applying the amount to any shift already carrying that shiftType (logged before the toggle, imported from .ics via the questionnaire at 3184, or added by a template/quick-fill). Only the delete path (4691) warns about repricing, which implies toggling off was meant to be display-only; the lab contradicts that. Either semantics is defensible; the two surfaces holding different ones is the defect.
failure: Log Mon–Wed 12h nights this period (or .ics-import them), then toggle Night off in Settings. Hero still prices them at $75.15/hr (night amount included, +$360 gross for the period). Open Patterns → 'Mon–Wed nights' preset anchored on the same week: it prices the identical three nights at $65.15/hr and shows a take-home per paycheck ~$280 lower than the hero for the same schedule.
fix: Pick one: (a) make hourlyRate/shiftGross treat `diff.active===false` as no differential so the calendar reprices to match the lab and the dimmed row (then the delete warning applies to toggling too, and the Settings hint should say so); or (b) drop the `active()` gate in patternCellShiftType so the lab prices what the calendar prices. (a) touches wage core; (b) does not, but leaves the toggle as pure decluttering. Either way add a probe covering an inactive differential on both paths.
dissent:
Verified the code (index.html:1119-1134 shiftGross/hourlyRate, 1202-1220 patternCellShiftType/patternCellToShift, 1257-1301 patternMetrics, 2636-2650 statOf, 4089-4104 AddShiftSheet, 4689-4692 tog/del) and the described mechanism is real but the "defect" framing doesn't survive scrutiny — it's a coherent, intended design, not a cross-surface contradiction.

The codebase draws one consistent line everywhere: `active` gates whether a *brand-new* shift instance can be created/classified under a given differential; it never gates the *pricing* of a shift that already carries that shiftType. That rule holds identically in every place a new shift is produced:
- Add-Shift sheet (line 4099): `differentials` filtered by `d.active` for the chip list offered for a *new* pick.
- Pattern Lab cell classification (patternCellShiftType, 1202-1211): a generic day/night cell resolves to 'base' instead of 'night'/'weekend-eve' when the differential is inactive — deciding what a *newly generated* cell becomes.
- AddShiftSheet's own live preview (4104) and statOf/calc (2646, and calc's analogue) do NOT check `.active` when pricing a shift that already has a concrete `shiftType` — by the same rule, because that shift isn't being newly created, it's being priced as recorded.

Deleting a differential (del(), 4691) is a materially different operation: it removes the key from `differentials` entirely, so `differentials[s.shiftType]` becomes `undefined` for every shift using it — hourlyRate then falls back to base for all of them, past and future, which is exactly why only *that* path warns about repricing. Toggling `active` off leaves the key (name/amount/type) intact, so already-tagged shifts keep pricing off the same, still-present definition — consistent with the general (undisputed) behavior that editing a differential's dollar amount immediately reprices every shift already tagged with that type. That's a feature, not the bug being described.

Crucially, the Pattern Lab's readout for a preset (patternMetrics, 1257-1301) never reads or reprices the shifts already on the calendar at all — it takes no `shifts` argument and computes purely from `pattern.cells` + the anchor date, generating hypothetical fresh shifts via `patternCellToShift` for a lcm(cycle,14)-day span. Opening 'Mon–Wed nights' after logging real Mon–Wed night shifts does not touch, reference, or reprice those logged shift records — it's an independent simulation of "if this preset were applied under current settings," reusing shiftGross/computeNet for calculation-methodology parity with the hero (per the comment at 1229), not for value parity with whatever happens to already be on the calendar. `planPatternApply` (1305) only consults `shifts` to decide skip-vs-replace placement, never to reprice; applying with replace=on would regenerate those specific days from scratch and only then would the calendar/hero converge with the lab's number, which is the expected lifecycle.

So the two 'surfaces' the finding pits against each other actually agree on both of the app's real rules (active gates new-shift classification; existing shiftType instances price off the persisted, non-deleted definition regardless of active). The apparent mismatch in the walkthrough is an artifact of comparing a real, already-logged shift against an unrelated hypothetical preset simulation for the same calendar dates — not a computation disagreement over the same data. This reads as intended, load-bearing behavior (mirrored by the explicit del()-only repricing warning) rather than a genuine defect.

title: Paystub import turns a premium-only earnings row into a negative differential
where: index.html:3386-3387 (applyPaystub) and index.html:3739-3745 (PaystubReview row rendering)
detail: applyPaystub derives each differential as `da = round((s.rate - p.baseRate)*100)/100` and stores it as the dollar amount with no floor and no cross-check against `s.earnings`. The parser's row regex (index.html:3360-3363) captures the HOURS AND EARNINGS 'Rate' column as `s.rate`. On PeopleSoft-style stubs (the very format this parser targets: 'Fed MED/EE', 'Fed OASDI/EE', 'TOTAL GROSS'), a shift-differential earnings code is frequently listed at the premium rate alone (e.g. 'PD Night Diff  4.00  36.00  144.00'), not the base-plus-premium rate. The review sheet renders the same `da` via `+$${da.toFixed(2)}/hr` with no guard, so the user is shown '→ Night  ·  +$-61.15/hr' and the Apply button writes it.
failure: Base rate $65.15 read from 'Pay Rate: $65.15 Hourly'; a row 'PD Night 4.00 36.00 144.00' classifies as 'night' and yields da = 4.00 - 65.15 = -61.15. Review sheet shows '+$-61.15/hr'; after Apply, every night shift prices at (65.15 - 61.15) = $4.00/hr, so a 12h night reads '+$48 gross' in the Add-Shift preview and the hero collapses accordingly.
fix: In applyPaystub (and the matching line in PaystubReview), treat a row whose rate is below the base rate as a premium-only line: `const da = s.rate < p.baseRate ? s.rate : s.rate - p.baseRate` (optionally confirmed by `Math.abs(s.rate*s.hours - s.earnings) < 1`), and never write a negative amount. Add a harness case with a premium-only row asserting the night amount lands at +4.00.
dissent: Mechanism is real but the finding's precondition is unshown for this parser and the outcome is not silent, so it does not earn a medium. Confirmed from the cited code: index.html:3386 computes `da = Math.round((s.rate-p.baseRate)*100)/100` with no floor and no earnings cross-check; PaystubReview :3739-3745 prints `+$${da.toFixed(2)}/hr` unguarded; and sanitizeData (:1041-1049) keeps any finite `amount`, so a negative would survive reload/sync. Granting all that, three things undercut it. (1) The parser is a single-stub parser, not a PeopleSoft-general one -- it hard-codes `PA W/H`, `PA PHILADELPHIA W/H`, `PA LS Tax`, `403(b)`, `Pay Rate: $X Hourly` and the `PD `/`Incentive - ` prefixes (:3345-3363). Its `rate - baseRate` model only ever worked for its one real user if that stub's PD rows carry the blended rate, so for the format it targets the outcome is the intended one. The finding's claim that PeopleSoft stubs "frequently" list the premium alone is asserted, not demonstrated against this stub; the harness has no differential-row fixture at all (`makeMinimalPdf` emits no pay data, BACKLOG.md:876), so nothing in the repo shows a premium-only row ever reaching this code. A stub from another payroll system is more likely to miss the `Pay Rate:`/`HOURS AND EARNINGS…TAXES` anchors entirely than to half-parse into this exact shape. (2) The outcome is visible before it is written: the review sheet shows "+$-61.15/hr" next to "$4.00/hr" under the explicit contract "Fix anything that looks off, then apply" (:3719), so it is a caught-at-review defect, not a silent corruption -- though the rows are not editable in-sheet, so the user's fix is Cancel or Settings afterward. (3) The surface is near-dead by the project's own record: exactly one successful paystub import in two months, and the scan was demoted to a secondary "instead" link (CLAUDE.md Product surfaces; BACKLOG.md:680,884). Nothing documents a negative differential as intended, so a zero-floor (`Math.max(0,da)`) or a "looks off" flag on a negative row is a legitimate P3 hardening nit; the proposed `rate < base ? rate : rate-base` heuristic silently rewrites the parser's model for an unverified format and touches displayed dollar figures, which the wage-core skill says needs its protocol. As filed -- medium, with a concrete hero-collapse failure -- it restates a speculative stub format as an observed defect.

title: "Take-home per paycheck" for cycles that don't divide 14 is an average that no actual paycheck ever equals, and nothing on screen says so

detail: patternMetrics prices the rotation over lcm(n,14) days and divides by span/14, so for any cycle length that is not 7 or 14 the figure is a mean across several different paychecks. title: Template-brush cells skip the weekend-differential inference the grid hint promises, and are indistinguishable from generic cells that get it
where: index.html:1204 (patternCellShiftType: `if(cell.kind==='fixed') return cell.shiftType;`); hint at index.html:4536; cellLabel/cellColor at index.html:4316-4326
detail: Generic Day/Night brushes resolve to weekend-day / weekend-eve on Sat/Sun (index.html:1205-1211). A cell painted with a template brush ('tpl:<id>', built at index.html:4350-4358 as kind:'fixed') keeps the template's shiftType verbatim, so a 'My nights' template (shiftType 'night') on Saturday is priced at the plain night differential. The hint under the grid reads, for every brush, 'Weekend days pick up your weekend differentials automatically.' Once painted the two cells are identical: cellLabel gives 'Night 12h from 7:00 PM' for both (differentials.night.name === 'Night'), cellColor gives differentials.night.color for both, same glyph. Ran it: Fri/Sat/Sun nights, 7-day cycle, $50 base, defaults -- generic brush: gross $4,632, net $3,324, calendar types weekend-eve/night/weekend-eve; template brush: gross $4,320, net $3,089, calendar types night/night/night. $312 per paycheck, ~$8.1k/yr, from a brush choice the UI says makes no difference. The exact-type semantics match calendar quick-fill (index.html:2922), so the arithmetic is deliberate; the hint and the indistinguishable cells are the defect.
failure: Nurse saves her usual 'Night 12h' template, paints Fri-Sun with it because it's the brush with her name on it, reads the hint that weekends pick up her weekend differentials, and the lab under-quotes her rotation by ~$312 per paycheck; after apply, every Sat/Sun shift on the calendar is typed 'night' rather than 'weekend-eve' and the hero agrees with the low number.
fix: Either (a) make the hint brush-aware and mark fixed cells (e.g. the ⚡ glyph or the template name in cellLabel) so a template-painted weekend visibly keeps its exact type, or (b) in patternCellShiftType let a fixed cell whose shiftType is 'base' or 'night' go through the same weekend inference as the generic kinds (an explicitly weekend-typed template still keeps its type). (b) changes displayed dollars via patternCellShiftType/planPatternApply, not the listed wage-core functions, but should still get a harness assertion (generic vs template brush on a Saturday).
dissent: Mechanism confirmed but the outcome is the documented template contract, not a defect. index.html:1204 returns cell.shiftType verbatim for kind:'fixed' cells; the section comment directly above it (~1138-1142) states the rule explicitly: "Generic 'day'/'night' cells resolve to the weekend differential when they land on a Sat/Sun (the same inference the .ics import uses); 'fixed' cells (built from a template) keep their shiftType." The app has exactly two weekend-inference sites (grep: .ics import at 902-916 and the generic brushes at 1205-1211); the manual Add-Shift sheet and calendar quick-fill (2922, spreads qfTemplate.shiftType literally) never infer. So the app-wide model is coherent: the app infers a type only where the nurse gave none, and anything she typed herself -- a saved template -- is literal everywhere. The finding's own "concrete failure" ("after apply ... the hero agrees with the low number") is exactly what quick-filling that same 'night' template onto a Saturday on the calendar already produces today; the lab is faithful to the template contract, not diverging from it. The finding concedes the arithmetic is deliberate and narrows itself to (1) the unconditional hint at 4536 and (2) painted-cell indistinguishability. (2) is by construction -- a fixed 'night' cell and an inferred 'night' cell are the same shift, and the brush chips themselves are visibly distinct ("⚡ <template name> ×12h" vs "☾ Night 12h"), so the nurse chose the template brush knowingly. (1) is a one-sentence copy imprecision written for the default generic brushes (initial brush is 'night12'); it is a P3 wording nit, not a [medium] wage-math finding worth "$8.1k/yr" framing. Proposed fix (b) would actually break the documented contract by making the lab retype a deliberately-'night' template on weekends while calendar quick-fill keeps it literal -- introducing the lab/calendar divergence the #65 design avoided. Not already in the backlog, but does not rise above a nit; if anything, file the hint wording ("generic Day/Night brushes pick up ...") as P3 polish.

title: poster_key is reversible: member user_ids and the board creator's id are readable, and the salt is a public constant
where: supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:59-69 ("see co-members" policy + full-table grants on swap_members and swap_groups), :158 (poster_key derivation); live-verified column grants on project mnnlgcxnvodjwlhhiphq
detail: Live, `authenticated` holds SELECT on swap_members(group_id, joined_at, user_id) and swap_groups(id, name, invite_code, created_by, created_at), and the "see co-members" policy returns every member row of every group the caller is in. swap_board() derives `poster_key = substr(md5(author::text || group_id::text || 'scrubpay-swaps'), 1, 8)`. The salt is a string constant in a public repo (github.com/patrick222-dotcom/705-v1 answers `"private": false`), group_id is known to every member, and md5 is a browser one-liner. So `supabase.from('swap_members').select('user_id,joined_at').eq('group_id',G)` yields the N candidate authors; hashing each gives a complete poster_key -> user_id table for the board. Binding a uuid to a person: swap_groups.created_by names the board creator outright (the one who sent everyone the link); joined_at orders the others against who-got-the-link-when; and a single confirmed match pins uid <-> display_name permanently (reveal returns post_id -> name and that post's key was on the board). The migration comment at :155-157 says "Not reversible" and the 2026-07-30 audit checked only that the `author` column can't be selected -- nobody tested rebuilding the key from readable columns. The client never selects from swap_members (only the insert at index.html:1706) and reads only id,name,invite_code (+ order by created_at) from swap_groups (index.html:1675, 1719), so both grants are pure over-exposure.
failure: A nurse posts "give up Fri 9/19 night" after the app tells her "Posted -- your unit sees it anonymously." (index.html:5062). Any co-member with devtools runs one REST select and one md5 loop and knows which uuid posted it; if she created the board, `created_by` names her with no inference at all. Every post she makes in that group is tagged to her from then on -- the feature's core promise is false.
fix: Step 1, grants only (no key change, no client change): `revoke select, update on public.swap_members from authenticated;` (keep insert -- the client's insert at index.html:1706 sends Prefer: return=minimal, and is_swap_member/join_swap_group run as definer) and `revoke select, update on public.swap_groups from authenticated; grant select (id, name, invite_code, created_at) on public.swap_groups to authenticated;`. Step 2: stop deriving the key from a public constant -- keep a per-group random secret in a table with no grants to anon/authenticated and read it inside swap_board (definer), so a leaked uid can never be turned into a key. Nothing persists poster_key client-side (it is recomputed from each board fetch), so changing the derivation has no data impact. Add two probes to the RLS audit: as member A, `select user_id from swap_members` must be 403; `select created_by from swap_groups` must be 403.

title: propose_swap never checks the caller is a leg: any member can reserve and hide any two posts on the board
where: supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:245-265 (propose_swap); live pg_get_functiondef is identical
detail: The RPC validates membership, 2-3 legs, and that each post is open and in the group -- but never that auth.uid() authors any of the legs. The only thing keeping proposals to "matches involving me" is the client: computeSwapSuggestions (index.html:1763-1835) only emits suggestions with a 'me' leg and doPropose (index.html:5079-5099) passes them through. Any member can call `supabase.rpc('propose_swap',{g, post_ids:[x,y]})` with any two open post ids returned by swap_board. Each call flips both posts to 'proposed': swap_board (:164) then hides them from everyone but their authors, openPosts (index.html:5302) drops them, and computeSwapSuggestions ignores them; the two authors get a "WAITING ON 2 OF 2 TO ACCEPT" card pairing them with a stranger's unrelated post. The proposer is not a party, so they can neither see nor decline it -- only the victims can (decline_swap_match) -- and the attacker re-proposes on the next 15s poll. No rate limit, no per-user cap on open matches, and status 'expired' exists but nothing ever sets it.
failure: One member with the invite code pairs every open post on the board in a loop from the console: the board reads "Nothing posted yet" for the whole unit and every poster is stuck declining nonsense matches that come straight back. Selectively: lock every other 'give' for Friday so only their own remains visible to the colleague who wants it.
fix: In propose_swap, after the foreach loop and before `return m`: `if not exists (select 1 from swap_match_legs where match_id = m and leg_user = auth.uid()) then raise exception 'not_a_party'; end if;` -- the exception rolls back the match, legs and status flips. Optionally cap concurrent 'proposed' matches per proposer (e.g. 5) in the same function. Add an audit probe: as member C, propose posts by A and B only -> must raise not_a_party and leave both posts 'open'.

title: Raw 'parties decline matches' UPDATE policy bypasses decline_swap_match and strands the other party's post as 'proposed' forever
where: supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:202-205 (policy), :233-235 (update (status) grant), :130 and :277-278 (why it is unrecoverable); live policy confirmed via pg_policies
detail: decline_swap_match() exists precisely so declining releases the reserved posts in one transaction (001:269-282). But the policy 'parties decline matches' plus `grant ... update (status) on swap_matches` still let any party `PATCH /rest/v1/swap_matches?id=eq.<m>` with `{status:'declined'}` directly. That path never touches swap_posts. Afterwards: the author's 'update own posts' USING requires status='open' (001:130) so she cannot withdraw or edit it; decline_swap_match raises match_not_proposed because status is already 'declined' (001:277-278); reveal_match raises match_not_proposed (001:315); the board RPC hides it from everyone else (001:164). The client only ever uses the RPC (index.html:1938-1944; the sole `.from('swap_matches')` is a select at :1882), so the raw path is pure attack surface.
failure: Colleague B, party to a match with A, sends one REST PATCH from devtools. A's give-up post vanishes from the unit's board, shows only in A's own list, cannot be withdrawn, edited or re-proposed, and never comes back -- A's shift is effectively un-swappable until the owner fixes the row in SQL.
fix: `drop policy "parties decline matches" on public.swap_matches; revoke update on public.swap_matches from authenticated;` (re-grant only `select (id, group_id, status, created_at)`). All declines then go through the security-definer RPC. Add an rls_audit assertion that a direct PATCH to status='declined' is 42501 for a party.
dissent: The mechanism is real but the failure path is not reachable in the shipped app and the stated damage does not materialise. (1) Reachability: the client's only `.from('swap_matches')` call is the SELECT at index.html:1882; decline goes exclusively through `supabase.rpc('decline_swap_match')` at :1941, so the raw PATCH is never issued by the UI. Reaching it requires an authenticated group member who is already a leg-party of the match (is_match_party = leg_user = auth.uid(), 001:189-191) to hand-craft a REST call with their own JWT -- and because they are a leg-party, their own post is a leg too, so the attack strands the attacker's post as much as the victim's. (2) Damage overstated: the finding says A's shift becomes "un-swappable until the owner fixes the row in SQL". It does not -- swap_posts has no unique constraint on (author, shift_date) (only the invite_code unique at 001:33 and the housekeeping index at :342), the "insert own posts" policy checks only author + membership (001:120-122), and the client insert at index.html:1737 has no already-posted guard, so A re-posts the same give-up shift in one tap. Residual harm is one stale 'proposed' row in A's own list plus a 'declined' match card -- clutter, not loss of function. (3) Context: the swap board has zero real groups (density currently zero per CLAUDE.md) and is de-emphasised by owner decision, so a medium-severity griefing vector that needs a malicious co-worker in her own invite-code unit is not worth a session against the sole production Supabase project. What survives is a low hardening nit, not a medium finding: the `update (status)` grant at 001:233-235 and the "parties decline matches" policy at :202-205 are vestigial (the comment "used by the ... decline flows" at :231 is stale since the RPC landed), and dropping both is a safe two-line change to fold into the next swap-board migration -- the RPCs are security definer and need no grant.

title: "Apply to my calendar" writes another member's unvalidated shift_meta into the victim's shifts
where: index.html:5280-5290 (doApplyPlan), specifically :5285
detail: shift_meta is free-form jsonb authored by another member: the insert grant (001:142-143) and policy (:120-122) accept any JSON under 500 bytes, including scalars, and match_details passes it through verbatim. doApplyPlan pushes `{shiftType:meta.shiftType, hours:meta.hours, start:meta.start}` straight into saveDayShifts -> setShifts (index.html:2857-2858) with no coercion; sanitizeData (:953-986) runs only on load. Until the next load the hero and breakdown compute `shiftGross(baseRate, differentials[s.shiftType], s)` (:1290, :2646, :2775, :2795) with whatever `hours` was sent: a string -> NaN, 1e6 -> millions, a scalar shift_meta -> undefined -> NaN; `h+=s.hours` (:2646) concatenates. The debounced save persists the row; on the next open sanitizeData (:976-977) drops it. Display-only helpers are safe -- giveMetaLine (:4067-4071) and fmtTime12 (:4039-4040, TIME_RE :738) coerce, so the board render itself cannot be crashed this way.
failure: After a confirmed pickup the nurse taps "Add to my calendar": the hero take-home reads "$NaN" (or an absurd figure) for the rest of the session, the malformed shift is synced to the cloud, and when she reopens the app the shift she just picked up is silently gone from her calendar.
fix: In doApplyPlan (before the push at :5285) accept incoming.shift_meta only if it is an object with `typeof shiftType==='string'`, `Number(hours)` finite and in (0,24], and `start` absent or matching TIME_RE; otherwise toast the existing "copy the plan instead" message and return. Server side, add a CHECK on swap_posts.shift_meta guarded by jsonb_typeof so the cast never throws: `shift_meta is null or (jsonb_typeof(shift_meta)='object' and jsonb_typeof(shift_meta->'shiftType')='string' and jsonb_typeof(shift_meta->'hours')='number' and (shift_meta->>'hours')::numeric between 0.1 and 24)`. Neither change touches shiftGross/hourlyRate/computeNet or the sanitizeData coercions.
dissent:
The mechanics are described accurately (doApplyPlan at index.html:5285 pushes meta.shiftType/meta.hours uncoerced; sanitizeData :972-982 only runs on load), but the failure path is not reachable through the shipped UI and the realistic impact does not justify a medium security finding.

1. The UI cannot produce malformed shift_meta. The only composer path (index.html:5049-5050) builds it from the poster's own calendar shift, which has already been through sanitizeData: shiftType is a string, hours is a finite number in (0,24], start is TIME_RE-valid. Reaching the failure requires a signed-in member of the victim's invite-code group to hand-craft a PostgREST insert (or an update while the post is still 'open' -- 001:126-130 freezes it once proposed), i.e. a hostile coworker bypassing the app.

2. The attacker must then get the victim to match against that post, every leg must accept -- which reveals the attacker's display name to the victim -- and the victim must tap Apply. Before she does, the malformed meta is rendered right beside the button via giveMetaLine (:5473-5476, :4067-4071): a scalar meta reads "Shift ×undefinedh", hours 1e6 reads "×1000000h", a non-numeric string reads "×abch". The only variant that renders innocuously is a numeric string ("12"), and that one is harmless: shiftGross (:1131) coerces it in multiplication, hourlyRate (:1120) already guards a missing differential, and sanitizeData coerces hours to Number on reload so the shift survives -- the worst artifact is `h+=s.hours` (:2646) showing "012" in a day total until the next load.

3. The persisted damage is self-healing by design: the blob save writes the row, and the next load's sanitizeData drops it -- the comment at :950-952 says this backstop exists precisely so string/NaN fields cannot corrupt calculations. "The shift she just picked up is silently gone" is a shift the attacker fabricated with garbage hours; there is no arrangement to lose, and the plan text tells her to confirm through the unit's normal process anyway. No anonymity break, no cross-user read, no persistent corruption, no wage-core involvement.

A colleague with group membership who wants to harm a coworker can post a well-formed fake give and simply not show up; forging JSON to make her hero read $NaN for one session, at the cost of de-anonymizing themselves, is not a threat worth an owner session. The 3-line guard in doApplyPlan is reasonable hygiene and could be filed as a P3 nit, but not as a medium security item with a server-side CHECK migration against the only (production) project.

title: MAX_BLOB_BYTES is enforced only in the browser; user_data.data has no server-side size bound, so one signed-in account can fill the shared free-tier database
where: supabase/migrations/000_core.sql:27 (data jsonb, no CHECK); confirmed live via pg_constraint — user_data carries only PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY and UNIQUE(user_id), no trigger. Client side: index.html:2464 (the only size check), index.html:2496 (pagehide flush) and index.html:2512 (retrySync) call saveToSupabase without it; saveToSupabase itself at index.html:1324-1344 does no size check.
detail: The 512KB cap that CLAUDE.md calls the 'free-tier guard' is a JavaScript comparison in the debounced save effect. The table has no `pg_column_size(data)` CHECK (compare `events.props`, which does have one in the same migration), and RLS only constrains *which row* an authenticated user may write, not *how big*. Since the Google OAuth app is In production, any Google account is a valid `authenticated` caller against the public anon key. Even inside the app the cap is not actually held: when the debounce path trips it, it toasts 'cloud sync paused' and returns, but the `pagehide`/`visibilitychange` flush (2496) and the manual retry (2512) both call saveToSupabase directly with the same oversized `snapshotRef`/`serializeState()` and write it anyway. Separately, the check compares `JSON.stringify(...).length` (UTF-16 code units) against a byte budget, so non-ASCII notes can be ~3x the intended bytes before it trips.
failure: A hostile (or merely curious) signed-in user issues `POST /rest/v1/user_data` (Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates, on_conflict=user_id) with the public anon key + their own JWT and `data` = tens of MB of random base64 (incompressible, so TOAST does not shrink it), repeating the update to leave dead tuples behind. Nothing in Postgres refuses it. The free-tier project crosses its 500MB database quota and Supabase drops it to read-only: every other user's `saveToSupabase` then fails on every edit, each device falls into the failed-save backup mode with the sync-error badge, and cross-device sync stops for everyone until the owner intervenes in the dashboard. In-app variant a real user would see: after the 'cloud sync paused' toast, backgrounding the tab silently uploads the oversized blob the toast just said was not being uploaded.
fix: Add migration 004 (000 is never back-edited): `alter table public.user_data add constraint user_data_data_size check (pg_column_size(data) <= 524288), add constraint user_data_data_is_object check (jsonb_typeof(data) = 'object');` — matches the pattern already used for `events.props`. Then move the size check into `saveToSupabase` itself (return null and logClientError when `new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(data)).length > MAX_BLOB_BYTES`) so the flush and retry paths share it, and treat a 23514 from the server like any other failed save (backup + syncError), which the existing branch already does.

title: ical-proxy accepts the public anon key: verify_jwt does not mean "signed-in user"
where: supabase/functions/ical-proxy/index.ts:8-9 and :46-59 (no role/user check anywhere in the handler); anon key shipped at index.html:616
detail: The function's header comment and CLAUDE.md both claim `verify_jwt` restricts the proxy to signed-in users ("an unauthenticated POST is 401, so it is not an open proxy"). That is only true for a request with NO Authorization header. The Supabase gateway's verify_jwt checks the signature, and the project's anon key is itself a JWT signed with the same secret (`role: anon`, exp 2036). Live probe against the deployed function (version 1, byte-identical to the repo copy): no header -> 401 UNAUTHORIZED_NO_AUTH_HEADER; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key from index.html>` with `{"url":"https://www.google.com/"}` -> 422 not_a_calendar, i.e. the handler ran and fetched the upstream. The handler never inspects the JWT's `role`/`sub` (index.ts:46-59 go straight from body parsing to the allowlist), so anyone who has viewed the page source can drive it. The allowlist still holds (169.254.169.254 -> 403), so this is not an internal SSRF, but the second allowlist entry `/^www\.google\.com$/` (index.ts:22) has no path constraint, so the project is an anonymous relay for arbitrary google.com URLs and any public/secret Google Calendar feed, with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (index.ts:31) so it works from any web page.
failure: A script with the anon key (harvested by any of the crawlers already hitting badgebudget.com) loops POSTs at a large public Google calendar feed: each call is a free-tier invocation plus up to 2MB of egress. The project hits the free-tier egress/compute cap, and every real nurse loses cloud sync and calendar sync until the next billing window, or the owner pays. The intended control ("only a signed-in user can call this") is simply not in force.
fix: In the handler, before the allowlist: read `req.headers.get('Authorization')`, decode the bearer JWT payload (the gateway has already verified its signature) and return 401 unless `payload.role === 'authenticated'` and `payload.sub` is a UUID; or equivalently build a supabase client with that header and require `auth.getUser()` to return a user. Then correct the two comments (index.ts:8-9, CLAUDE.md Supabase section) and add the negative test to the ship ritual: `curl` with the anon key must return 401. While there, pin both Google entries to the `/calendar/ical/` path prefix so `www.google.com` is not a general-purpose relay.

title: Previous account's secret feed URL survives a stalled sign-out and is shown/saved for the next account on the same device
where: index.html:2529-2540 handleSignOut (does not clear icalSub/icalUrl/hydratedUserId/icalSyncedForUser); index.html:2335-2340 resetToDefaults (same omission); index.html:2441 hydration effect `catch(_){ return; }`
detail: The only place `icalSub`/`icalUrl` are cleared on sign-out is the SIGNED_OUT branch of onAuthStateChange (index.html:2417). `handleSignOut` exists precisely because that event "won't fire if signOut stalled" (its own comment) and it mirrors the branch for every field except the four iCal ones; `resetToDefaults` (which it calls) also skips them. So after a stalled sign-out (the WebKit lock deadlock this codebase already documents) user A's bearer credential stays in React state. When user B signs in on the same tab, hydrateFromCloud sets hydratedUserId, the effect at index.html:2431-2450 calls loadIcalSub(B); if that throws (network blip) it `return`s before the `setIcalSub(sub); setIcalUrl(...)` line, leaving A's URL and subscription object in place. Settings renders the CALENDAR SYNC block for any truthy `user` (index.html:4785) with `value={icalUrl}` (4790), 'Sync now' calls runIcalSync which resolves `url` from `icalSub.icalUrl` (3254), and 'Update link' calls saveIcalSub(user.id=B, url=A's) (3300). Even on the success path there is a render window between setHydratedUserId(B) and loadIcalSub resolving where B's Settings shows A's URL.
failure: On a shared unit iPad: nurse A signs out (sign-out stalls, 3s timeout), nurse B signs in on flaky Wi-Fi so loadIcalSub fails. B opens Settings and sees A's secret Google Calendar address in the input; tapping 'Sync now' pulls A's shifts into B's questionnaire; tapping 'Update link' stores A's feed under B's account permanently, so B's app re-fetches A's private calendar on every open from then on.
fix: Add `setIcalSub(null); setIcalUrl(''); setHydratedUserId(null); icalSyncedForUser.current = null;` to handleSignOut (or into resetToDefaults, which both sign-out paths call). In the hydration effect, make the catch clear state too (`setIcalSub(null); setIcalUrl('');`) instead of returning with whatever was there, and key the effect so a stale subscription from a different uid can never be reused: in runIcalSync/onSaveIcalUrl, refuse when `icalSub.userId !== user.id` (store the uid on the icalSub object). Harness: seed state as A, simulate a rejected signOut and a rejected loadIcalSub for B, assert the input is empty.

title: Google sign-in runs the OAuth *implicit* flow, not PKCE — tokens land in a URL fragment that stays one Back-press away in browser history
where: index.html:610-615 (createClient with no options) and index.html:4619-4625 (handleGoogleAuth / signInWithOAuth)
detail: CLAUDE.md and the invite-link comment at index.html:1602-1605 ("supabase-js PKCE puts its own `?code=` here") both say the Google path is PKCE. It is not. The vendored supabase-js 2.45.4 (auth-js 2.65.0) sets `DEFAULT_AUTH_OPTIONS={autoRefreshToken:!0,persistSession:!0,detectSessionInUrl:!0,flowType:"implicit"}`, and `createClient(url, key)` at 610-615 passes no `auth` options, so `signInWithOAuth` sends no code_challenge and Supabase redirects back to `redirectTo` with `#access_token=…&refresh_token=…&provider_token=…` in the fragment. auth-js consumes that fragment and clears it with `window.location.hash=""` (verified in the bundle; the PKCE branch instead does `searchParams.delete("code")` + `history.replaceState`). The clear happens only after an awaited `/auth/v1/user` round-trip, i.e. normally after the page's `load` event — and I verified in the sandbox Chromium (iPhone 13 profile) that a post-load `location.hash=''` grows `history.length` 2→3 and `history.back()` restores the full `#access_token=…&refresh_token=…` URL. (When the round-trip beats `load`, Chromium converts it to a replacement and no entry is left — so it is timing-dependent, not guaranteed.) The fragment refresh token stays valid until the first rotation (~1h) or a server-side sign-out.
failure: A nurse signs in with Google on a shared unit workstation or a borrowed phone, then walks away. Whoever next touches the browser presses Back (or opens History) and sees `badgebudget.com/#access_token=…&refresh_token=…` in the address bar; pasting that URL into a tab (or calling /auth/v1/token with the refresh_token) gives them her session and her pay history for up to an hour, and a colleague scrolling the shared machine's history days later still sees the tokens in the list even after they have expired.
fix: Opt into PKCE: `window.supabase.createClient(url, key, {auth:{flowType:'pkce'}})` at index.html:611. auth-js then returns `?code=` and scrubs it with replaceState (no history entry, no token in any URL); `takeSwapInviteFromUrl` (1619-1629) already writes foreign params like `code` back byte-identical, so the invite flow is unaffected. Re-run the smoke suite's sign-in section and confirm a real Google sign-in on badgebudget.com still lands (the redirect allow list is unchanged). Then correct the PKCE claim in CLAUDE.md → Auth and the comment at 1602-1605.

title: client_error batch can exceed the live `events_props_check` (< 2000 bytes) and is silently dropped after the ring buffer was already cleared
where: index.html:1443-1456 (flushClientErrors) with index.html:1385-1398 (track) and the live constraint `events_props_check CHECK (pg_column_size(props) < 2000)`
detail: `flushClientErrors` ships up to `ERR_FLUSH_CAP`=8 entries, each with a 300-char `msg`, 80-char `src`, `t` and `line`. Measured in the live database: 8 entries at 300 chars = 3,116 jsonb bytes; 6×300 = 2,348; 8×200 = 2,316; 8×170 = 2,060 — all rejected by the CHECK; 5×300 = 1,964 and 8×120 = 1,676 pass. So any batch of ≥6 max-length entries, or 8 entries averaging ≳165 chars, fails with 23514. Max-length entries are the normal case for the errors that matter: `ErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch` (index.html:2160) logs `error` plus the JSON-stringified `errorInfo` (a componentStack of hundreds of chars, sliced to 500 in the buffer and 300 in the flush), and PostgREST error objects mirrored from `console.error('Load error:', error)` (1469) run 150-300 chars. `track()` swallows the rejection into `console.debug` (1396), which is not mirrored into the ring buffer, and `__takeErrorLog()` (567-572) already removed the batch before the send — so the loss is total and self-concealing. Live data so far: 11 client_error rows, max 526 bytes, max n=3, so nothing has been lost *yet*; the arithmetic is deterministic for the first bad session.
failure: A nurse hits a React render crash loop (ErrorBoundary fires several times) or a run of failed cloud loads during one visit. On her next app open the flush builds an 8-entry, ~3 KB batch, Postgres rejects it, the ring buffer is already empty, and the owner's `select … where name='client_error'` shows nothing for exactly the session that needed diagnosing — worse than before the telemetry existed, because the local buffer was also drained.
fix: Budget the payload in `flushClientErrors` before calling `track`: cut per-entry `msg` to ~160 chars and drop the oldest entries while `JSON.stringify(props).length > ~1700` (jsonb adds ~5-10% over the text form, so 1,700 text bytes stays under 2,000). Optionally also widen the CHECK in a `004` migration (e.g. `< 4000`) so a stale client can't lose a batch either. Add a smoke assertion that seeds 8 long entries into `scrubpayErrors` and asserts the resulting event body is under the cap.

title: Hero's 'See the full breakdown' / 'Share BadgeBudget' links accidentally inherit the full .hero card style, ballooning them and adding dead scroll space to the very first screen
where: index.html:3491-3492 (className="hero more linklike"); CSS: .linklike padding:0 at 79, .hero padding/border-radius/background/box-shadow at 114, .hero .more at 119
detail: The two footer buttons are given className="hero more linklike" — three independent classes, not a scoped ".hero .more" selector. Because the token "hero" is also the class name of the enclosing card, both buttons literally match the top-level `.hero{background:var(--ink);border-radius:22px;padding:22px 24px;...box-shadow:...}` rule (line 114) in addition to `.hero .more` (119) and `.linklike` (79). `.hero` and `.linklike` have equal CSS specificity (one class each), so the tie is broken by source order, and `.hero` (declared later, at line 114) beats `.linklike`'s `padding:0` (line 79) — the buttons keep `.hero`'s 22px/24px padding, border-radius and box-shadow instead of being flush, padding-free text links. Verified live on an iPhone-13 viewport: document.querySelectorAll('.hero') genuinely returns 3 elements (the card plus both buttons); each button's computed style is 'padding: 22px 24px', height balloons to 59px, and a screenshot shows each rendering as its own visible dark rounded pill with an inset highlight seam nested inside the real hero card, rather than a plain link line.
failure: On every load, the hero card — the first thing a nurse sees, and the thing the whole app is built around — is roughly 120px taller than intended, almost entirely padding around two one-line links. One-handed on a phone, that's extra scrolling distance before she reaches the calendar / '+ Log a shift' controls beneath it, and the two links visually read as broken/unstyled boxes rather than the intended small footer actions.
fix: Stop reusing the literal token "hero" as a class on these buttons — give them a distinct class (e.g. "hero-more") so they no longer match the card-level .hero rule, or restructure so the descendant relationship is expressed purely through DOM nesting rather than a repeated class name.

title: Dollar-amount edit fields in Settings (differential rate, savings-goal target) have a 17px-tall tap target, versus 44px used everywhere else in the same sheet
where: index.html:4715 (differential amount NumInput) and 4754 (goal target NumInput); CSS: .drow .amt / .drow .amt input at 312-313, .danger-link at 423
detail: `.drow .amt{padding:5px 10px}` wraps the number, but `.drow .amt input{width:54px;border:none;background:transparent;...}` sets no padding or min-height on the <input> itself, and the wrapper is a plain <span> (not a <label>), so tapping the padded pill around the number does nothing — only the number glyph itself is live. Measured live in the rendered Settings sheet on an iPhone-13 viewport: each goal-target and differential-rate NumInput is 54x17px (34x17 for a multiplier-type differential), and the adjacent 'Del' button on the same row is 35x39px — both well under the 44px minimum the codebase otherwise enforces (33 other spots in index.html explicitly set minHeight:44), and in visible contrast to the compliant ~42px-tall .inp input fields (line 292, padding:13px 14px) used for base rate, tax %, and bonus $ a few rows above in the same form.
failure: Correcting a savings-goal target or a shift differential's dollar rate one-handed mid-shift means landing a tap inside a 17px-tall strip — under half the app's own stated minimum — and the larger padded pill around it looks tappable but isn't, so a mistap lands nowhere and she has to try again to get the cursor into the number field. The 'Del' button on the same row is likewise a few pixels short of 44px in each dimension.
fix: Give .drow .amt input real padding or min-height:44px so the live hit-box matches the visible pill (or turn the .amt span into a <label> so tapping anywhere in the pill focuses the input), and bump .danger-link to a 44px box on these money-editing rows to match the convention used elsewhere in the file.

title: Calendar scroll box has an absolute 420px height floor that exceeds the entire viewport in landscape
where: index.html:184 (.cal-vscroll), contrast with .sheet/.modal at index.html:396,399
detail: `.cal-vscroll{max-height:60vh;min-height:420px;...}` sets a hard 420px minimum height on the Month-view scroll box, in plain (non-dynamic) `vh`. Elsewhere in this same file the sheet/modal containers were deliberately switched to `dvh` (`.sheet{max-height:92dvh}` line 396, `.modal{max-height:90dvh}` line 399) specifically because mobile browser chrome changes available height — the calendar container is the one scroll surface that was never brought in line with that pattern, and unlike them it also carries a bare pixel floor with no viewport-relative cap under it.
failure: Rotate an iPhone 13 (the project's own test profile) to landscape while on Month view. Landscape viewport height for a phone is typically ~350-390px after Safari's toolbar, well under the 420px the calendar box is forced to occupy. The calendar's own scroll container alone now consumes more vertical space than the entire screen, pushing the greet-row/hero, the +Log a shift button and the bottom nav completely off-screen — a one-handed nurse who rotates her phone (even accidentally) has to scroll the whole page up and down just to see anything besides the calendar grid, including controls that were one glance away in portrait.
fix: Cap `.cal-vscroll` against the real viewport instead of a fixed px floor — e.g. drop `min-height:420px` (or express it as `min(420px, 60dvh)`) and switch `60vh` to `60dvh` so the box shrinks with the actual available height in landscape the same way `.sheet`/`.modal` already do.

So even granting the 420px floor exceeds landscape viewport height, the described outcome is just 'the user scrolls the whole page' — which is exactly how a page taller than the viewport is supposed to behave, not a trapped/unreachable UI. title: Pay-period stepper's scroll animation ignores prefers-reduced-motion

detail: The ‹/› pay-period stepper in the greet row calls movePeriod, which calls scrollFocusToDate, which drives the calendar's scroll position with animateScrollTop — a hand-rolled requestAnimationFrame loop that eases el.scrollTop over 380ms. The entire calendar viewport still animates a smooth 380ms scroll to the new period's position — exactly the kind of scrolling motion the reduced-motion setting exists to suppress, and exactly the kind of thing this same file is careful to suppress for boot timers/CSS transitions elsewhere.

title: Month/Year view control uses role="tablist"/"tab" without the tab keyboard pattern

title: The month-scroll container isn't keyboard-scrollable on its own
where: index.html:3561 (`<div className="cal-vscroll" ref={monthScrollRef} onScroll={onMonthScroll}>`)
detail: `.cal-vscroll` is a nested `overflow-y:auto; max-height:60vh` scroll region (index.html:184) holding 16 months of day-cell buttons. It has no `tabIndex` and no keydown handler, so it is never itself a focus stop and never responds to arrow/Page keys. The outer page (`body`/document) is what actually scrolls when a keyboard-only user (no mouse/touch — e.g. a switch or keyboard-only sighted user, not necessarily a screen-reader user) presses Page Down/Space with focus elsewhere on the page; that scrolls the page around the calendar card, not the calendar's own internal 60vh viewport.
failure: A sighted keyboard-only user wants to browse forward from the current month inside the calendar card without a pointer device. There is no key they can press with focus inside the calendar region to page the 60vh scroller itself — their only route is Tab-ing individually through every day-cell button in the current month (up to ~31 Tab presses) until focus-follows-into-view scrolls the next month into range, which works only as an incidental side effect of tabbing through unrelated buttons, not as an intentional "scroll the calendar" action.
fix: Give `.cal-vscroll` `tabIndex={0}` (and ideally an `aria-label`, e.g. "Calendar months") so it becomes a standard scrollable region that responds to the browser's native arrow/Page/Home/End key scrolling once focused.
dissent: The cited code is accurate — .cal-vscroll (index.html:3561-3562) indeed has no tabIndex or keydown handler — but the "failure" doesn't actually block a keyboard user from reaching or browsing the calendar. Every day cell inside .cal-vscroll is itself a focusable <button> (rendered via MonthSection), so a keyboard-only user reaches every month exactly as WCAG 2.1.1 requires: by Tabbing through the day-cell buttons, with the browser auto-scrolling the nested .cal-vscroll region into view as focus moves — the same behavior any scrollable list of focusable controls exhibits (an inbox, a select menu, a virtualized list). An explicit tabIndex={0} scroll wrapper is the fix for a container whose content is NOT independently focusable (e.g. static images/paragraphs); here it is. The finding concedes as much ("works... as an incidental side effect of tabbing through unrelated buttons") but mischaracterizes ordinary focus-follows-scroll as a defect rather than the expected mechanism. Nothing is unreachable — worst case is it takes more Tab presses than a sighted mouse user's Page Down, which is a minor UX nit at most, not a WCAG failure, and isn't a new class of issue beyond the already-filed calendar-virtualization backlog item.

title: Add-Shift sheet has no dialog semantics, unlike every sibling sheet in the same file
where: index.html:4164 (AddShiftSheet's outer <div className="sheet">)
detail: Every other modal sheet in the app declares role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="..." on its .sheet element: the feedback sheet (line 2057, aria-label="Send feedback"), the .ics import-confirm sheet (3820, "Confirm schedule import"), the classify-imported-shift sheet (3848, "Classify imported shift"), and both swap sheets (5311/5330, "Shift swaps"). AddShiftSheet's own <div className="sheet"> at 4164 carries none of these. There is also no Escape-key handler anywhere for this sheet (the only keydown listener in the whole app is the account menu's, lines 1966-1968) or focus management on open/close.
failure: A screen-reader user who opens 'Add a shift' from a calendar day gets no announcement that a dialog named 'Add a shift' just opened, and the assistive-tech virtual cursor is free to wander into the calendar/dashboard behind the scrim while it is nominally modal — the exact opposite of what happens one sheet over (Import/Classify/Feedback/Swaps) for the identical visual pattern. The same user also has no keyboard way to dismiss it (Escape does nothing here, though it works for the account menu).
fix: Add role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Add a shift" to the .sheet div at line 4164, matching the existing pattern, and give it the same document keydown Escape->dismiss() handling already implemented for the account menu (1966-1968).

title: Every 'Remove' button for a logged shift shares the identical accessible name
where: index.html:4200 (inside the list.map over `list` in AddShiftSheet)
detail: `<button className="danger-link" onClick={()=>remove(s.id)}>Remove</button>` renders once per entry in `list`, and the UI explicitly supports multiple shifts logged on one day (the whole 'ON THIS DAY' section exists for that). Every one of those buttons has the literal accessible name 'Remove', with no reference to which shift. The same component already knows how to disambiguate an equivalent case: the template-delete button a few dozen lines earlier is `aria-label={'Delete template '+t.name}`.
failure: A screen-reader user who has logged two shifts on the same day (e.g. a regular shift plus a picked-up OT shift) hears 'Remove, button' twice with nothing to tell them apart, and can only guess which one their focus is currently on.
fix: Give each Remove button a distinguishing aria-label, e.g. aria-label={'Remove '+(differentials[s.shiftType]?.name||s.shiftType)+' ×'+s.hours+'h shift'}, mirroring the 'Delete template '+t.name pattern already used in the same file.

title: Pattern Lab's dialog has no dialog role, no aria-modal, and no accessible name — unlike every sibling sheet
where: index.html:4417-4419 (list mode) and index.html:4486-4488 (edit mode), function PatternLab
detail: PatternLab's outer markup is `<div className="scrim" onClick={dismiss}><div className="modal" onClick={e=>e.stopPropagation()}>...`. Neither the scrim nor the modal div carries `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, or an `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`. Every other overlay in the app that plays the same role does carry this: FeedbackSheet (`role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Send feedback"`, line 2057), the confirm dialog (`role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"`, line 2138), the ICS import confirm (line 3820) and classify-shift (line 3848) sheets, and SwapsSheet (lines 5311, 5330) all declare it. PatternLab is the odd one out even though it visually looks and behaves like the same kind of sheet.
failure: A VoiceOver/NVDA/TalkBack user taps 'Patterns' in the topnav (openPatternLab, line 2933). No 'dialog' role is announced and no name is given for what just opened — the screen reader has no signal that a new modal context replaced the page, and (because there is no aria-modal) it does not treat the rest of the page as hidden, so rotor/browse-mode navigation can wander into the calendar and topnav that are still present in the accessibility tree underneath.
fix: Add `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` and an `aria-label` (e.g. "Pattern lab" / "Edit pattern") to the `.modal` div in both the list-mode and edit-mode returns, matching the convention already used by FeedbackSheet/SwapsSheet/the ICS sheets.

title: Pattern Lab has no focus trap and no Escape-to-close, so keyboard focus leaks into the obscured app behind it
where: index.html:4300-4581 (function PatternLab, no keydown handling or focus management anywhere in the component); index.html:2596-2600 (body-scroll lock is the only 'modal open' side effect); index.html:1966-1968 (Escape-to-close exists for the account menu, for contrast)
detail: There is no `useEffect`/`addEventListener('keydown', ...)` and no ref-based focus trap anywhere in PatternLab (confirmed by reading lines 4300-4420 and grepping the whole component body). The app never uses `ReactDOM.createPortal` (grep returns nothing) and never sets `inert` or toggles `aria-hidden` on background content when a sheet opens — the only 'a modal is open' side effect anywhere in the app is `document.body.style.overflow='hidden'` at line 2598, which blocks page scroll but does nothing to the DOM's tab order or accessibility tree. Meanwhile the account menu two thousand lines earlier (lines 1966-1968) does register a document keydown listener that closes on Escape, showing the app knows how to do this and simply didn't do it here.
failure: A keyboard user opens Pattern Lab, then presses Shift+Tab from the '×' Close button (aria-label="Close", line 4419) — focus moves backward into whatever topnav/calendar control precedes PatternLab in the DOM (e.g. the 'Patterns'/'Swaps'/'Settings' topnav links or a calendar day cell), all of which are still fully interactive but visually hidden under the `.scrim` overlay (`rgba(18,18,26,.55)` + blur, line 394). The user sees no focus indicator at all (it's under the overlay) and can activate a background control — e.g. re-triggering `openPatternLab` or opening Settings underneath the already-open Pattern Lab — while apparently still 'inside' Pattern Lab. Separately, pressing Escape while Pattern Lab is open does nothing at all; the only ways to close it are clicking the × button or clicking the scrim backdrop.
fix: Give the modal a focus trap (cycle Tab/Shift+Tab within its own focusable elements) and move focus onto it when it opens (e.g. the close button or heading), restoring focus to the invoking control on close; add a `keydown` listener for `Escape` that calls `dismiss()`, matching the pattern already used for the account menu at line 1966.

title: The 'Put it on the calendar' apply preview updates silently for screen-reader users
where: index.html:4566-4572 (the `.preview` div inside PatternLab's apply flow); contrast with index.html:3457 (`aria-live="polite"` on the analogous pay-period label)
detail:
`applyPlan` (a `useMemo` over `applyStart`, `applyWeeks`, `applyReplace`, defined at lines 4312-4314) drives a plain `
` at lines 4566-4572 that reports 'This adds N shift(s) · ', how many days were skipped, and how many will be replaced. Changing the Starting date input, the 'FOR' week-count buttons, or the Replace toggle recomputes this text, but the div carries no `aria-live` region. Elsewhere in the same file the app already uses `aria-live="polite"` for exactly this kind of 'a control changed and this readout updated' case (the pay-period `{periodLabel}` at line 3457).
failure: A screen-reader user changes 'FOR' from 6 weeks to 12 weeks, or flips 'Replace shifts already on those days' on, expecting to hear the updated add/skip/replace counts the sighted preview shows immediately. Nothing is announced — they have to manually re-navigate to the preview div after every change to learn whether their pattern will now replace shifts or add fewer than expected, which is exactly the kind of consequential, silent state change AA's programmatic-status guidance (and the app's own precedent at line 3457) exists to prevent.
fix: Add `aria-live="polite"` (and ideally `aria-atomic="true"`) to the `.preview` div at line 4567 so the recomputed adds/skipped/replaced counts are announced whenever `applyStart`, `applyWeeks`, or `applyReplace` change.

title: Onboarding step transitions never move focus and use no heading markup
where: index.html:5704-5835 (all 5 obStep branches), goObStep index.html:2198-2201, exit-to-app at index.html:3081/3391/3412
detail: Every step change in the wizard (welcome -> base-rate -> differentials -> taxes -> done, the back button, and the final exit into the main dashboard when setupComplete flips to true) is a full React remount of a different JSX subtree in the same container. None of the five branches use an <h1>-<h6> for its question/heading text ("What's your base hourly rate?", "How does your pay change by shift?", etc. are all plain <div className="q">), there is no ref.focus()/autoFocus placed on any heading or first control after a transition, and no aria-live region wraps the step content. grep -n "<h1\|<h2\|<h3\|<h4" confirms zero headings anywhere inside Onboarding().
failure: A VoiceOver or NVDA user taps 'Get my estimate' (index.html:5729). The button they were focused on is unmounted and replaced by the base-rate step; the browser silently drops focus to <body> (or leaves it nowhere useful), and nothing is announced. The user hears nothing happen and has no heading to jump to with the AT's heading-navigation shortcut (H in NVDA/JAWS, rotor in VoiceOver) -- they must re-explore the whole page from the top to discover the new question exists. This repeats at every one of the 5 steps and again on the transition out of onboarding into the live app.
fix: Give each step's question a real heading (e.g. <h1 className="q">), and on obStep change move focus to that heading (or the step's first control) via a ref + useEffect keyed on obStep. Same treatment for the setupComplete flip into the main app.
dissent: The technical claim is accurate (verified: no h1-h6 in Onboarding(), no ref.focus()/useEffect on obStep, no aria-live) but this restates a known, already-accepted class of finding rather than surfacing new information. CLAUDE.md's own KNOWN list already documents an equivalent-severity, same-root-cause a11y gap (the account menu's role=\"menuitem\" without roving-tabindex) and explicitly reasons it away as consistent with the rest of the app: 'it isn't worth a focus manager the rest of the app doesn't have either (no sheet traps focus).' Onboarding's lack of focus management on step transitions is the identical architectural gap applied to a different component — not a newly discovered defect. The 'high' severity is also overstated for a linear 5-step wizard with a visible progress bar and no branching, where AT users still encounter new content via normal tab/swipe navigation; this is degraded UX, not a broken/inaccessible flow. Filing it as a new high-priority finding would be re-flagging a design tradeoff the project has already made and documented, wasting the owner's time re-litigating it under a different file name."

title: 'ESTIMATED' tax-rate tag fails WCAG AA contrast
where: index.html:328 (.tag.est rule), rendered at index.html:5796 and index.html:5798
detail: .tag.est{color:#C2820A;background:#FDF3DD} at 10.5px/600-weight. Computed contrast of #C2820A on #FDF3DD is 2.93:1 -- well under the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal text (it doesn't even clear the 3:1 large-text bar, and 10.5px isn't large text anyway). This is the badge sitting directly on 'Federal income tax' and 'State tax' in the onboarding taxes step (obStep 3), the two rates that feed the projected take-home figure shown one step later.
failure: A low-vision nurse using the taxes step at obStep 3 cannot read the word 'ESTIMATED' next to Federal/State tax -- it visually all but disappears against its own pill background, so she can't tell which of the pre-filled numbers are guesses she should check versus fixed values (FICA's .tag.auto pill, by contrast, passes at 4.75:1).
fix: Darken #C2820A (or lighten the pill background) until contrast clears 4.5:1 -- e.g. swap to the same indigo-on-indigo-soft treatment already used for .tag.auto, or darken to roughly #8A5A05 on the existing #FDF3DD.

title: Gross-pay summary line on the 'done' screen falls just under AA contrast
where: index.html:5823
detail:
{sample.hours} hrs · 6 shifts · gross {fmt(sample.gross)}
sits inside the card whose background is var(--ink-2) = #21242F (index.html:5820). Computed contrast of #7E8290 on #21242F is 4.04:1, below the 4.5:1 AA requirement for 13px/500 (normal) text. This is the one line on the onboarding completion screen that literally states the gross-pay figure.
failure: A low-vision user finishing onboarding sees the projected take-home number clearly (mint on ink-2, 8:1) but the supporting 'X hrs · 6 shifts · gross $Y' line next to it is noticeably harder to read -- it's the exact figure a nurse would want to sanity-check against her own math, and it's the weakest-contrast text on the screen.
