title: Onboarding back button has no accessible name
where: index.html:5739
detail: <button className="back" onClick={()=>setObStep(obStep-1)}>‹</button> -- the only content is the raw '‹' glyph; no aria-label, no title, no visually-hidden text. The visually identical arrow glyphs used for pay-period navigation in the main dashboard do carry one: aria-label="Previous pay period" / "Next pay period" (index.html:3457).
failure: A screen-reader user on the base-rate, differentials, or taxes step reaches the top-left button and hears only 'button' or an unhelpful glyph reading ('single left-pointing angle quotation mark, button') with no indication it goes back a step, unlike every other chevron button in the app.
fix: Add aria-label="Back" (or a dynamic 'Back to <previous step>') to the Head component's back button, matching the pattern already used for the pay-period nav arrows.

title: Dismissing the est-banner removes the focused control with no focus handoff
where: index.html:3471-3474 (banner buttons), index.html:2991-3001 (clearSample)
detail: Both dismiss paths -- 'Got it' (setEstimateMode('')) and 'Clear the sample' (clearSample(), which also ends in setEstimateMode('')) -- cause the entire `{estimateMode && <div className="est-banner">...}` block, including the very button just activated, to unmount. Neither path moves focus anywhere afterward (clearSample's confirmAsync dialog autoFocuses its own Confirm button while open, per index.html:2143, but once confirmed and the dialog+banner both unmount, nothing receives focus).
failure: A keyboard or screen-reader user who presses 'Got it' (or confirms 'Clear the sample') has focus silently dropped to <body> with no announcement that the banner is gone or where to go next -- they lose their place on a page that just changed shape under them.
fix: After clearing estimateMode, move focus to a stable nearby landmark (e.g. the hero take-home heading) with a ref + effect, so focus lands somewhere meaningful rather than being dropped.

title: Settings modal has no dialog semantics and its close button has no accessible name
where: index.html:4694-4697 (Settings)
detail: Settings renders as `<div className="scrim"><div className="modal">...<button className="back" onClick={onClose}>{Ic.x}</button>` with no role="dialog", no aria-modal, no aria-label/aria-labelledby on the modal, and the close button wraps only the bare Ic.x SVG (index.html:603, a <path> with no <title>, no aria-hidden) with zero text or aria-label. Every sibling sheet in the same file gets this right at the same call-site shape: FeedbackSheet (index.html:2057, 2059) has role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Send feedback" plus aria-label="Close" on its X button; SwapsSheet (index.html:5311, 5305) and the ICS import sheets (index.html:3820,3822 / 3848,3850) do the same. Settings is the one modal in this slice missing all of it.
failure: A screen-reader user (VoiceOver/NVDA/TalkBack) opens Settings from the account menu (the only route to Settings on a phone per the top-bar note in CLAUDE.md). Nothing announces that a dialog opened - no 'dialog' role, no name - so the user has no orientation cue and, because there's no aria-modal, can swipe/Tab straight past the sheet into the calendar/hero content still sitting behind the scrim. When they do reach the X button in the header, it announces only 'button' with no label, so they cannot tell it closes Settings; the only other way out is the 'Done' button at the very bottom of a long, multi-section scrolling sheet (goals, differentials, taxes, calendar sync), which they may never discover.
fix: Add role="dialog" aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby pointing at the "Settings" title div (or aria-label="Settings") to the .modal div at 4696, and add aria-label="Close" to the back button at 4697 - matching the pattern already used by FeedbackSheet/SwapsSheet/the ICS sheets in this same file.

title: ShareSheet has no dialog role or accessible name for the region
where: index.html:5682-5688 (ShareSheet)
detail: ShareSheet's outer sheet div (`<div className="sheet" onClick={e=>e.stopPropagation()}>`) carries none of role="dialog", aria-modal, or aria-label/aria-labelledby, even though its own close button (line 5687) does have aria-label="Close" and the visible title 'Share BadgeBudget' (line 5686) exists as plain text. This is the same gap as Settings but only on the region-level semantics, not the button.
failure: A screen-reader user tapping the Settings 'Show a QR code or send a link' button gets no announcement that a modal/dialog opened, and can navigate (swipe/Tab) into the app content behind the scrim since aria-modal is absent - the same background-leak problem as Settings, just without the extra unlabeled-button issue.
fix: Add role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Share BadgeBudget" to the sheet div at line 5683, consistent with FeedbackSheet/SwapsSheet in the same file.

title: Differential name-edit input has no accessible name
where: index.html:4714 (Settings differentials row)
detail: `<input className="nm" value={d.name} disabled={k==='base'} onChange={...} style={{...}}/>` has no wrapping <label>, no aria-label, no placeholder, and no id/htmlFor pairing. Every other input in this same Settings screen (name, base rate, tax fields, new-differential/new-goal inputs) carries either an aria-label or at minimum a placeholder; this one field - the only in-place editor for an existing differential's name - has neither.
failure: A screen-reader user tabs to this field while editing a custom differential (e.g. one named 'Charge') and hears only 'edit text, Charge' with no field name, so on a row where they haven't just heard the adjacent toggle (which does carry aria-label={d.name}) they cannot tell this control is the differential's name versus any other text field on the page.
fix: Add aria-label={d.name + ' name'} (or similar) to the input at index.html:4714.

title: Duplicate, context-free "Del" button labels in differentials and savings-goals lists
where: index.html:4716 and 4755 (Settings)
detail: Every per-row delete control in both the differentials list and the savings-goals list renders `<button className="danger-link" onClick={...}>Del</button>` with no aria-label distinguishing rows. A user with 4 differentials and 3 goals ends up with 7 buttons that all have the identical accessible name 'Del'. Differential deletion is gated by confirmAsync (index.html:4691, names the differential in the confirmation copy), but delGoal (index.html:4687) deletes immediately with zero confirmation.
failure: A screen-reader user navigating Settings via the rotor's 'buttons' list (which strips surrounding row context) cannot tell which 'Del' belongs to which goal or differential. For goals specifically, since there is no confirmation step, activating the wrong one in that list permanently deletes the wrong savings goal with no undo.
fix: Give each delete button a distinguishing aria-label, e.g. aria-label={'Delete '+d.name+' differential'} at 4716 and aria-label={'Delete '+g.name+' goal'} at 4755; consider also gating delGoal behind confirmAsync to match the differential-delete pattern.

title: SwapsSheet dialog claims aria-modal but has no focus trap, no initial focus, and no Escape handler
where: index.html:5330 (and :5311 signed-out variant) — SwapsSheet's role="dialog" aria-modal="true" wrapper
detail: SwapsSheet renders `<div className="sheet" ... role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Shift swaps">` (index.html:5330; signed-out gate identical at :5311) but nothing in the component manages keyboard focus: no ref/useEffect moves focus into the dialog on open (grep of the whole 4819-5659 body finds only one unrelated `autoFocus`, on the display-name input at :5356, and the single `useRef` in the file, :4873, is for a stale-reveal timestamp, not focus), no keydown handler traps Tab inside the sheet, and no Escape handler exists anywhere in SwapsSheet (the only 'Escape' handler in the whole file is AccountMenu's, index.html:1966-1969, scoped to that component's own `open` state). Because `showSwaps` is rendered mid-tree inside App's JSX (index.html:3642-3647), after the main calendar content and the `+ Log a shift` FAB (index.html:3608-3609) which precede it in DOM order, the live page behind the scrim is never removed from the tab sequence.
failure: A keyboard user (or screen-reader user driving via Tab) opens Shift swaps (topnav 'Swaps' or the Home card button at index.html:3596), lands on the sheet's Close button (index.html:5305, the first focusable element in the dialog) and presses Shift+Tab once: focus jumps out of the dialog entirely and onto the `+ Log a shift` FAB (index.html:3608), a fully live, visibly-covered-by-the-scrim button. Pressing Enter there opens the Add-Shift sheet stacked on top of the swap board, even though `aria-modal="true"` asserts the rest of the page is inert. Symmetrically, Tab forward past the sheet's last control (e.g. the composer's 'Post to the board' button at :5653, or '+ Join another board' at :5587) leaves the dialog instead of wrapping back to Close — a keyboard user loses their place with no way back except tabbing all the way through the hidden background page. There is also no way to dismiss the sheet from the keyboard except tabbing all the way to the Close button and activating it, since Escape is not wired up here.
fix: Add a mount-time effect that moves focus to the dialog (or its first control) and a keydown handler on the sheet that (a) calls onClose on Escape and (b) cycles Tab/Shift+Tab between the sheet's first and last focusable elements (a small focus-trap utility, reused by the other `role="dialog"` sheets at :2057, :3820, :3848 which have the identical gap).

title: Withdraw/Decline confirm dialog (used by the reveal-flow actions) has no Escape handler and lets Tab escape the dialog
where: index.html:2127-2148 (ConfirmHost), invoked from SwapsSheet's doWithdraw (:5069) and doDecline (:5155)
detail: `confirmAsync(...)` — the confirmation shown for 'Withdraw this post?' (index.html:5069) and 'Decline this proposed swap?' (index.html:5155) inside the matching/reveal flow — renders `role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"` (index.html:2138) with only two buttons: Cancel then Confirm (`autoFocus`, index.html:2143). autoFocus correctly seeds initial focus on Confirm, but there is no keydown handler anywhere in ConfirmHost, so Escape does not dismiss it, and Tab forward from the auto-focused Confirm button (the last element inside the dialog) is not intercepted, so focus leaves the dialog into whatever follows ConfirmHost in the document instead of cycling back to Cancel.
failure: A nurse using the keyboard to decline a proposed swap (index.html:5155) reaches the confirm dialog, and either presses Escape expecting it to cancel (it does nothing — the destructive choice stays on screen with no keyboard-conventional way to back out) or tabs forward from the focused Confirm button and lands outside the alertdialog entirely, again with the modal claim unmet.
fix: Give ConfirmHost the same Escape-to-cancel keydown handler AccountMenu already has (index.html:1966-1969), and trap Tab between Cancel and Confirm.

title: Render-blocking boot scripts prevent any paint (even the splash) until 5 cross-origin CDN fetches resolve
where: index.html:17-21 (script tags), index.html:487 (#splash), index.html:490-592 (boot watchdog)
detail: The 5 CDN scripts (React, ReactDOM, Babel standalone, pdf.js, supabase-js) are classic <script src> tags in <head> with no async/defer, spanning 3 third-party origins (unpkg.com x2, cdnjs.cloudflare.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net). Per HTML parsing rules the browser must fetch+execute all 5 sequentially before continuing to parse the rest of <head> (the ~460-line <style> block) and reach <body> — so neither the #splash placeholder nor the boot watchdog script (which starts the 8s timer) can run until all 5 have loaded or errored.
failure: On a slow or filtered connection (e.g. locked-down hospital Wi-Fi) where one of these 3rd-party origins stalls, the user sees a fully blank white tab with zero feedback — no spinner, no watchdog message — for as long as that network fetch hangs, because the watchdog's own 8s clock cannot start counting until the parser reaches the boot <script> tag, which requires all 5 earlier blocking scripts to have already resolved.
fix: Add a minimal inline watchdog/fallback at the very top of <head>, before the 5 CDN script tags, so a loading/stalled-connection fallback can appear independent of whether those specific network fetches ever complete; alternatively investigate defer + Babel-standalone's DOMContentLoaded auto-transform to unblock initial parsing.

title: Scrolling the calendar past a pay-period boundary fires a real Supabase write
where: index.html:2735-2748 (onMonthScroll -> setPPS), 2291-2295 (serializeState includes payPeriodStart), 2453-2487 (debounced save effect, payPeriodStart is a dependency at line 2487, and the body at 2459-2479 saves unconditionally once hydrated with no check that anything besides the view state changed)
detail: payPeriodStart is part of the persisted blob (serializeState) and is a dependency of the 500ms-debounced cloud-save effect. onMonthScroll (a scroll-settle handler on the month view) calls setPPS(ps) whenever the scroll-follow logic decides the visible row belongs to a different pay period (line 2746: `if(ps && ps!==payPeriodStart) setPPS(ps)`). That state change alone re-triggers the save effect, and the effect has no content-equality guard against what was last written (unlike the 15s poll's own normalize() check at 2550/2560) - it only checks blob size and hydration status before calling saveToSupabase. So a signed-in user who just scrolls the month calendar to look at a future/past period, with no edits at all, produces a real network upsert to user_data roughly once per period boundary crossed (throttled only by the 500ms debounce and the 180ms scroll-settle timer).
failure: A nurse casually scrolling through several months on her phone (checking a coworker's request, planning ahead) causes a burst of Supabase writes and a flashing 'Syncing...' indicator (line 3442) purely from browsing, once per pay-period boundary she scrolls past - wasted battery/data and free-tier write volume for a pure read/navigation action, and it also bumps updated_at, which can make a second signed-in device's 15s poll believe a real edit just landed when only the view moved.
fix: Either drop payPeriodStart from the debounced-save trigger (persist the viewed period separately, e.g. only on pagehide/sign-out, or fold it into an existing save rather than scheduling a new one), or apply the same normalize()-style content-equality check the poll already uses (comparing serialized data with payPeriodStart zeroed out) before calling saveToSupabase, so a save that would be byte-identical is skipped.

title: pagehide/visibilitychange flush silently drops an edit when the best-effort save fails
where: index.html:2489-2505 (flush), contrast with the debounced save effect's failure handling at index.html:2470-2479; saveToSupabase at index.html:1324-1344
detail: The debounced save effect explicitly guards against a failed cloud write: when saveToSupabase(...) resolves null (it always resolves, never throws — see the catch at 1339-1343 and the error branch at 1337), the else branch at line 2478 calls writeBackup(user.id, dataToSave) so the edit survives locally under BACKUP_KEY. The separate `flush` handler registered for `pagehide`/`visibilitychange`→hidden (added specifically because '500ms debounce would otherwise drop it', per the comment at 2489) does not do this: its call chain is `saveToSupabase(...).then(ts=>{ if(ts){ ...clear backup... } })` — the `if(ts)` guard only handles the success path. When `ts` is null/falsy (network drop, RLS/Postgres error, or the fetch simply being torn down mid-flight as the page actually unloads), the `.then` body does nothing: no writeBackup call, no error surfaced.
failure: Signed-in user edits a shift, then immediately backgrounds or closes the tab (the debounce hasn't fired yet, which is exactly the case this handler exists for) on a flaky connection. The pagehide-triggered save fails; because flush's failure branch is a no-op, the edit is written to BACKUP_KEY nowhere, never reaches Supabase, and — once the tab is actually gone — no longer exists in memory either. On the next load, hydrateFromCloud finds no newer backup and no newer cloud row, so the edit is gone with no toast, no syncError, and no recovery path, unlike every other save-failure path in the app.
fix: Mirror the debounced effect's failure handling in flush: when saveToSupabase resolves falsy, call writeBackup(snap.user.id, snap.data) just like line 2478 does. Because a `.then()` callback isn't guaranteed to run once actual page teardown begins, prefer writing the backup synchronously before firing the best-effort save (optimistic backup, cleared only on confirmed success) rather than only in the async continuation.
dissent: The asymmetry the finding describes is real (index.html:2496 has no writeBackup on a null result; 2478 does) and it is not in the KNOWN list or BACKLOG.md. But it is not a data-loss defect of the shape or severity claimed. (1) The flush is layered on top of the debounced save, not a replacement for it: on visibilitychange→hidden the 500ms timer at 2452 is still pending and is not cancelled. On desktop it fires within ~1s (throttled); on iOS it fires the moment the tab is foregrounded again. That path then does the full failure handling — writeBackup + setSyncError(true) — so the "no toast, no syncError, no recovery" claim is false for every background-and-return case, which is the common phone gesture. The edit is only unrecoverable if the OS discards the suspended tab before it is ever resumed, on top of a failed network write, on top of the edit having landed in the final 500ms. (2) On real pagehide (tab closed), the `.then` continuation is precisely the code that is not guaranteed to run during teardown — the finding concedes this — so adding an else-branch there does not close the window; the flush is explicitly best-effort ("best-effort immediate cloud save", 2495) and when it fails the user is exactly where they would be with no flush at all: the last <500ms edit before closing is lost. That is the pre-existing, inherent limit of a 500ms debounce, not a regression introduced by the flush handler "dropping" anything. (3) The remaining fix — an optimistic synchronous backup before every flush — changes the documented meaning of BACKUP_KEY ("written ONLY when a cloud save fails, so it always holds work the cloud never received", 2270-2272) on the hydrate path that once ate 47 days of shifts; it is a small hardening idea, not a high-severity integrity bug, and not something to schedule on the strength of a narrowed-down last-half-second-offline-then-discarded scenario. At most a P3 note for a dedicated sync session, if ever.

title: "Take-home per paycheck" is a cycle-average, shown with full confidence, for the exact rotations where real paychecks diverge from it

detail: patternMetrics averages gross/net over lcm(cycle,14) days and divides by (span/14) periods to get periodGross/periodNet/periodHours (1294-1298). The average of a real 14-day paycheck window over a periodic on/off sequence is invariant to which phase of the cycle a given real paycheck lands on ONLY when the cycle length divides 14 evenly (i.e. cycle ∈ {2,7,14} within the allowed 2..42 range) — because only then does every non-overlapping 14-day window contain the same whole number of full cycles. For every other cycle length — which includes the built-in 'weekend'-adjacent choice of 28 days in PATTERN_CYCLE_CHOICES (1146) and, most visibly, the shipped preset '4 on, 4 off nights' (id 4on4off, cycle:8, index.html:1163-1164) — consecutive real 14-day paychecks contain a DIFFERENT number of actual shifts depending on where the cycle's phase falls, so the true paychecks alternate above and below the displayed average rather than matching it. Concretely, for the 4on4off preset with the app's own default baseRate 65.15 and night differential +10 (index.html:2204, 688), a 12h night shift grosses 75.15*12=$901.80 (shiftGross, 1125-1133). Over the lcm(8,14)=56-day span (4 periods) the real per-period shift counts are 8,8,6,6 (28 total, matching 7 cycles * 4 shifts/cycle) — i.e. real paychecks alternate between ≈$7,214 and ≈$5,411 gross (a ~$1,800 swing), while the lab shows one flat number: the average of those, ≈$6,313. Every actual paycheck a nurse who applies this pattern receives will be either noticeably higher or noticeably lower than the number she was shown before committing to the rotation — exactly the kind of surprise the app's whole premise ("know what a shift is worth before it's worked") exists to prevent. The code's own comment at 1254-1256 calls this averaging 'an honest per-paycheck figure,' but nothing in the UI tells the user it's an average: the yearly figure is explicitly hedged with '≈' (line 4542, '≈ {fmt(metrics.yearNet)} a year') while the much more decision-relevant per-paycheck figure right next to it, and in the pattern list card and side-by-side comparison table, carries no such hedge anywhere.
failure: A nurse opens Pattern lab, picks the built-in '4 on, 4 off nights' preset (or types a custom 28-day cycle), sees 'Take-home per paycheck: $X' with no qualifier, and applies it to her calendar planning around that number. Her first real paycheck comes in ~$900-1,800 different (net) from what she was shown, with no warning that the number she budgeted against was ever anything but a fixed promise for every check.
fix: Qualify periodNet/periodGross/periodHours the same way yearNet already is — at minimum prefix them with '≈' in all three surfaces (index.html:4428, 4447, 4540-4542) whenever metrics.drifts is true or, more precisely, whenever cycle length doesn't evenly divide 14, and add one line under the money block naming that real paychecks will alternate (e.g. 'averaged — cycles that don't line up with a 2-week pay period pay more some checks and less others'). This is a display-only change in PatternLab and doesn't require touching patternMetrics's math, though a stronger fix (surfacing the actual min/max per-period swing) would.

fix: Either compute the welcome-screen figure the same way sampleNet() does (call the existing sampleNet-equivalent logic against current default state, which is already in scope at obStep 0) so the two screens can never drift apart again, or replace the literal '$3,951' with a value that is verified to match sampleNet()'s output under the current defaults. Do not hand-tune the string again without re-deriving it — that is how it went stale.

title: "Clear the sample" removes the seeded shifts but leaves the placeholder $65.15/hr rate in place with no indication it isn't real, once the honesty banner is gone
where: index.html:2991-3000 (clearSample), index.html:3408-3412 (finish('sample')), index.html:2231 and 969 (estimateMode is the only signal that the rate is fake)
detail: finish('sample') (line 3408-3412) sets `baseRate` to the placeholder 65.15 and seeds sample shifts, marking the state as fake only via `estimateMode:'sample'`. The est-banner (line 3464-3475) offers two exits when estimateMode==='sample': 'Enter my rate' (opens Settings) and 'Clear the sample' (calls `clearSample`). `clearSample` (line 2991-3000) strips the SAMPLE_PATTERN_ID-tagged shifts and unconditionally does `setEstimateMode('')` — it never checks whether the user actually entered a real base rate first. There is no other field anywhere (grep confirms `estimateMode` is the sole indicator) distinguishing 'nurse's real $65.15/hr' from 'never-touched placeholder $65.15/hr'.
failure: A nurse taps 'Show me an example' to see how the app works, then taps 'Clear the sample' directly (never 'Enter my rate'). The seeded shifts vanish and the banner disappears — but baseRate is still the fictitious 65.15. Every shift she now logs herself computes gross/take-home/hero figures against that fake rate with no banner, no warning, and nothing in the UI distinguishing it from a confirmed real rate. This state also serializes into the cloud blob and localStorage (serializeState includes baseRate and estimateMode='' ), so it persists across sessions and devices silently. The app's headline numbers are now systematically wrong for her actual pay, with the one mechanism designed to flag that (the est-banner) already dismissed.
fix: Track whether the base rate was ever explicitly set by the user (independent of estimateMode), or make `clearSample` refuse/redirect to rate entry when `baseRate` still equals the untouched sample default, so clearing the sample can never silently promote a placeholder rate to authoritative status.

title: Editing a savings goal's target down to $0 in Settings makes the Add-Shift preview show "Infinity%"
where: index.html:4248 (AddShiftSheet preview) / index.html:4686 & 4754 (Settings updGoalTarget + NumInput)
detail:
In Settings' SAVINGS GOALS list, each goal's target is edited with `<NumInput value={g.target} onCommit={v=>updGoalTarget(g.id,v)} min={0} .../>` (index.html:4754), and `updGoalTarget=(id,v)=>setGoals((goals||[]).map(g=> g.id===id ? {...g, target:parseFloat(v)||0} : g))` (index.html:4686) has no floor above 0. NumInput's own commit logic (index.html:4020-4028) sets the value to `min` (i.e. 0) whenever the field is cleared and blurred, or the user simply types 0. So a goal that already exists with a positive target can be driven to `target:0` entirely from the UI, live, in the same session — no reload and no pass through `sanitizeData` in between (Settings and AddShiftSheet share the exact same top-level `goals` state, wired at index.html:3617 and index.html:4677).

The forward per-shift preview at index.html:4247-4248 computes `const pct=Math.round(previewNet/g.target*1000)/10; const n=Math.ceil(g.target/previewNet);` guarded only by `previewNet>0` — there is no `g.target>0` check here (unlike the Settings reverse-view at index.html:4748, which does guard with `per>0 && g.target>0`, and unlike `sanitizeData`'s goals filter at index.html:1069-1081, which explicitly drops any goal whose `target` isn't a finite positive number specifically "so a malformed value can't yield NaN percentages in the shift preview"). With `g.target===0`, `previewNet/g.target` is `Infinity` in JS (positive/0), so `pct` is `Infinity` and the template literal renders the literal string "Infinity%".
failure: 1) Open Settings → SAVINGS GOALS, tap into an existing goal's amount field, clear it (or type 0) and tap/tab away so it blurs — the goal's target silently becomes $0, with no error or warning. 2) Close Settings and open the Add-Shift sheet for any day with a shift that has nonzero take-home. The goal line at the bottom of the shift preview reads e.g. "toward your goal: House down payment Infinity% (≈0 shifts)" — a glaringly broken, alarming figure shown right next to the take-home dollar amount the app exists to make trustworthy.
fix: Guard the AddShiftSheet goal line the same way the Settings reverse view already does — skip (or filter out) any goal whose `target` is not finite and > 0, e.g. change the `.map` at index.html:4248 to filter `goals.filter(g=>g.target>0)` before computing pct/n, or add `g.target>0 &&` inside the per-goal computation. Ideally also stop `updGoalTarget` from ever committing a non-positive target in the first place (e.g. clamp to the previous value, or require target>0 the same way `addGoal` already does at index.html:4684-4685), since that closes the root cause rather than just the one downstream symptom.

title: Swap board lets a nurse commit to a shift with zero indication of what it pays
where: index.html:3643 (SwapsSheet call site), 4819 (SwapsSheet signature), 5505-5531 (SUGGESTED FOR YOU cards), 5079-5099 (doPropose), 4067-4072 (giveMetaLine)
detail:
SwapsSheet is invoked at index.html:3643 with `user, shifts, dayEvents, notes, saveDayShifts, differentials` — no `baseRate`, no `keepRatio`, no tax inputs. Compare the sibling sheets at the same call-site block: AddShiftSheet gets `baseRate={baseRate} keepRatio={keepRatio}` and PatternLab gets `baseRate={baseRate} taxes={taxInputs}`. SwapsSheet structurally cannot compute a dollar figure for anything it shows, because it was never given the numbers to do it with. Its own comment at giveMetaLine (4066: "wage-free by construction — shift_meta never carries $") makes this deliberate for the *data model* (correct: differing bonus/OT status shouldn't transfer between nurses), but it also blocks the client-side display, which has nothing to do with the anonymity model and could safely use the viewer's own baseRate/differentials the same way AddShiftSheet already does (previewGross/previewNet at 4104-4105).
The result: the 'SUGGESTED FOR YOU' cards (5505-5531) render PICK UP / TRADE / 3-WAY SHUFFLE suggestions as date + shift-type + hours only (`describeLeg`, 5509) and a bare 'Propose' button (5527) that calls doPropose (5079) straight into `proposeSwapMatch`, which freezes the posts. Nothing between seeing the suggestion and committing to it ever calls `shiftGross`/`computeNet` on the incoming shift.
failure: A nurse opens Swaps, sees 'PICK UP · Fri Sep 19 · Night ×12h' and taps Propose. Once the other party accepts, the match is confirmed and effectively irreversible except through a Decline that the app itself frames as a social cost ('The others involved will see it fell through', 5155). Only after fully committing — accepting, revealing names, and tapping 'Add to my calendar' (doApplyPlan, 5260) — does she discover, via the Planner hero, what that shift actually pays. She had no way to compare this pickup against staying home, or against another posted shift, before agreeing to it. This directly contradicts the app's own stated promise, verbatim at the welcome screen ('Know your real take-home before you pick up the shift', line 5718) and the share blurb ('see what a shift is really worth before you pick it up', line 5667) — and it's inconsistent with the app's own established convention of surfacing $/hr specifically to 'compare pickups at a glance' (AddShiftSheet, line 4246), a convention the swap board's literal 'PICK UP' feature doesn't follow.
fix: Pass `baseRate` and `keepRatio` (or the fuller `taxes`, matching PatternLab) into SwapsSheet, and render an estimated take-home (or at minimum ≈$/hr) on each suggestion card and open board post using the viewer's own rate — the same `shiftGross`/`computeNet` calls AddShiftSheet already makes, applied to `shift_meta` — before the Propose button, not after acceptance. This adds a new displayed dollar figure, so it should go through the wage-core protocol (baseline probes, a new assertion, the deployed-build equality check) even though it doesn't touch shiftGross/computeNet/calc themselves — flagging wageCore for that reason.

title: privacy.html misdescribes sign-in as Google-only and claims no password is ever stored, but email/password is the app's primary, first-shown auth path
where: privacy.html:89-91 ("Your account" section) vs index.html:4584-4671 (AuthModal), specifically handleEmailAuth at index.html:4591-4613
detail: privacy.html says: "Sign-in uses Google. BadgeBudget receives your email address and name from Google and stores no password." But AuthModal (index.html:4584) renders an email+password form (the <form onSubmit={handleEmailAuth}> block, index.html:4638-4651) ABOVE the "or" divider, with "Continue with Google" as the secondary option below it (index.html:4658-4661). handleEmailAuth calls supabase.auth.signUp({email,password}) or supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({email,password}) (index.html:4600-4602) -- Supabase Auth stores a (hashed) password for every such account. `git log -S"signInWithPassword"` shows this path was added 2026-08-23 (PR #45), three weeks before privacy.html was written/last-updated 2026-09-07 (PR #78), so this isn't stale copy that predates the feature -- the notice was written after the feature existed and still doesn't mention it.
failure: A nurse who reads privacy.html before signing up, sees 'stores no password', and then creates an account via the email+password form (the first, more prominent option in the modal) has just had a password stored by the service, contradicting what she was told. She also isn't told BadgeBudget/Supabase directly receives and stores the email address she typed (the notice frames email receipt as something that only happens 'from Google'). This is a factual misstatement about data handling on the one page whose job is to state that accurately, and the same page backs the Google OAuth consent screen the owner is trying to get brand-verified.
fix: Update the "Your account" section of privacy.html to disclose both auth paths: e.g. "Sign-in uses Google OAuth or email/password, your choice. With Google, BadgeBudget receives your email address and name and stores no password. With email/password, your password is stored (hashed) by the auth provider (Supabase) -- BadgeBudget's own code never sees or stores it in plain text." No app-code change needed; this is a documentation-accuracy fix, not a wage-core or telemetry-code change.

title: privacy.html claims the anon_id device identifier 'is not linked to your name' — track() writes it into the same row as user_id for every signed-in action
where: privacy.html:104-107 vs index.html:1385-1397 (track()), exercised by ~25 call sites passing user?.id (e.g. 2859 shift_saved, 2912 template_applied, 3392 paystub_imported, 5063 swap_posted)
detail: privacy.html's Usage analytics section says events carry 'the page path, your browser's user-agent string, and a random device identifier generated in your browser. That identifier is not linked to your name and is not shared with anyone.' But track(name, props, userId) (index.html:1385-1397) always sets both anon_id:anonId() and user_id:userId in the SAME row, and the overwhelming majority of call sites pass userId=user?.id whenever the visitor is signed in (shift_saved, template_saved, swap_posted, pattern_saved, etc.). auth.users (which user_id foreign-keys into) holds the signed-in person's email and, for Google sign-in, name. CLAUDE.md's own dashboard spec confirms this join is actually performed operationally: the 'segment' classification tags a device 'insider' by matching 'any anon_id ever seen signed in as' the owner's or Courtney's account — i.e. the anon_id-to-identity join privacy.html says doesn't happen is precisely what the project's own ops tooling does.
failure: Once a signed-in nurse does anything tracked (saves a shift, applies a template, posts a swap), her per-device anon_id sits in the same events row as her user_id. Anyone with database access (the owner, who already runs 'select ... from events' per the documented Owner-read queries) can trivially resolve that user_id to her email/name via auth.users — the exact linkage the privacy notice tells her doesn't happen.
fix: Rewrite the disclosure to state accurately that once signed in, the device identifier can be associated with the account (matching actual, intentional behavior used for the insider/public segment split), rather than asserting it is never linked to identity.

title: privacy.html's Feedback section omits that a signed-in submitter's account id is always attached, regardless of the optional contact field
where: privacy.html:117-119 vs index.html:2006-2045 (FeedbackSheet submit) and 1354-1371 (submitFeedback)
detail: privacy.html says: 'If you use the feedback button, your message is stored along with the page you were on and your browser's user-agent string. An email address is optional — supply one only if you want a reply.' This frames identification as opt-in via the 'contact' field. But FeedbackSheet's submit (index.html:2043) calls submitFeedback({..., userId:(user&&user.id)||null}), and submitFeedback (1354-1371) writes that straight into feedback.user_id whenever the person is signed in — independent of whether 'contact' is filled in.
failure: A signed-in nurse who deliberately leaves the optional contact field blank, believing (per the notice's framing) that doing so keeps her feedback unattributed, has her account id stored on the row anyway — the row is linkable to her account from the moment it's inserted, contact field or not.
fix: State plainly that feedback submitted while signed in carries your account id on the row in addition to whatever you put in the optional contact field, so 'optional... only if you want a reply' isn't read as 'optional... only way to be identified'.

title: Add-Shift preview, calendar day cells, goal lines and the weekend-night card use a keep-ratio that omits percent custom withholdings, so they disagree with the hero and the pattern lab
where: index.html:2819-2820 (keepRatio) -> consumers at 4104-4105 & 4245-4248 (AddShiftSheet preview + goal line), 3919 & 3933 (Calendar day cell), 4747 (Settings '≈ N typical 12h shifts'), 3434 & 3512 ('Pick up a weekend night?' card)
detail: The hero (calc, 2787-2810) and the pattern lab (patternMetrics 1298) both price take-home through computeNet(), which subtracts customWithholdings — including type:'percent' ones computed on incomeTaxBase (1243). Every other take-home figure in the app is previewGross*keepRatio, and keepRatio = 1 - (federalTaxRate+stateTaxRate+ficaForPreview)/100 knows nothing about customWithholdings. Omitting the flat per-period deductions from a per-shift marginal figure is defensible; omitting a percent withholding is not — it is a per-dollar rate that applies fully at the margin. Reproduced with the extracted functions: base $50, fed 12, state 2.5, standard FICA, one custom withholding {Pension, 5, percent}, one 12h base shift in the period -> hero net 437.10 (Keep 73%), lab periodNet 437.10, Add-Shift previewNet 467 (implied keep 78%), day cell ~$467. Settings' goal line even claims to be 'the same per-shift take-home the Add-Shift preview uses' (4745-4746) — it is, and both are off from the hero. Hero and lab agree with each other; the preview family is the wrong one. (A related but separately-scoped omission was also raised: keepRatio also ignores flat pretax/posttax deductions the hero subtracts per paycheck, which is more defensible as a marginal-pricing choice once the paycheck already covers those flat amounts — the percent-withholding gap above has no such defense.)
failure: A nurse whose Settings carry a percent 'Other withholding' (e.g. a 5% 403b) logs one 12h day shift: the hero says $437 take-home this period and the lab says $437 / paycheck for a one-shift fortnight, but the Add-Shift sheet for that exact shift says 'about +$467 take-home', the calendar cell shows ~$467, and a $5,000 goal reads '≈ 11 typical 12h shifts' in Settings and in the preview when the hero's rate needs 12. Every pickup she evaluates is overstated by the withholding percentage.
fix: Fold the percent withholdings into keepRatio at 2820: const pctCW = (customWithholdings||[]).reduce((a,w)=> a + (w.type==='percent' ? (parseFloat(w.amount)||0) : 0), 0); const keepRatio = Math.max(0, 1 - (federalTaxRate+stateTaxRate+ficaForPreview+pctCW)/100). All five consumers then agree with computeNet at the margin. Add a harness assertion that, with a percent withholding set, Math.round(previewGross*keepRatio) === Math.round(computeNet(previewGross, taxInputs).net) when pretax/posttax are 0. Not an Invariant-3 function, but it changes displayed dollars, so run the wage-math probes and the deployed-build equality check.
dissent: The arithmetic is accurate but the failure path is not reachable through the shipped UI. `keepRatio` (index.html:2820) does omit `customWithholdings`, and `computeNet` (:1243) does subtract percent ones on `incomeTaxBase` — so IF state held a percent custom withholding, the Add-Shift preview (:4105), day cells (:3919/:3933), Settings goal line (:4747) and weekend-night card (:3434) would diverge from the hero/lab. But nothing in the app can put one there. `setCW` is invoked in exactly two places: `applyData` on load (:2318) and the clear-all reset to `[]` (:2338). It is passed into `SettingsSheet` as a prop (:3633/:4676) and never called — the Settings region (:4676–4800) contains no custom-withholding editor; the only "withholding" control is the FICA type/percent pair (:4731–4733). The paystub extractor (:3330–3400) maps a 403(b) line to `pretaxDeductions` (a flat dollar amount, which the finding itself concedes is defensibly excluded at the margin) and FICA to `ficaRate`; it never emits `customWithholdings`. Onboarding and the Add-Shift sheet don't touch it either. So the finding's scenario — "a nurse whose Settings carry a percent 'Other withholding' (e.g. a 5% 403b)" — names a control that does not exist; a real 403b lands in pretax dollars, not a percent withholding. The only routes to a non-empty `customWithholdings` are Import JSON (:4772 → `importData` :3074 → `applyData`) of a hand-edited file (the app's own export always carries `[]`), a direct localStorage/DB edit, or a legacy blob from a hypothetical earlier editor (pickaxe on the shallow 55-commit history finds none, and the 3 `user_data` rows are all builders). The finding's own repro was "with the extracted functions", i.e. synthetic state fed straight to the math, not the UI. Net: the whole `customWithholdings` feature is dormant (sanitized, priced by `computeNet`, shown as the $0 "Other withholdings" breakdown row at :3987, but with no input), so hero, lab and the preview family agree for every state the app can produce. At most a low note to fold percent withholdings into `keepRatio` if an editor ever ships — not a [high] displayed-dollar disagreement.

title: Add-Shift sheet defaults to the Night type even when Night is switched off — sheet and hero pay a differential the lab prices at base
where: index.html:4077 (`useState('night')`), with 4099 (`active` chip filter), 4104-4105 (preview), 4108-4109 (`draftShift`/`add`), vs 1198-1207 `patternCellShiftType`
detail: AddShiftSheet initialises `shiftType` to the literal `'night'` and never reconciles it with the `active` list it renders chips from. Settings lets a nurse toggle any differential off (`tog`, index.html:4690). When Night is inactive: no SHIFT TYPE chip is highlighted (the chip row only maps `active`), yet `previewGross` is still `shiftGross(baseRate, differentials['night'], draft)` — `hourlyRate` (1119-1124) never looks at `active` — so the preview prices a Night shift, and the primary button on a fresh day commits `draftShift()` with `shiftType:'night'`. The hero then prices that shift with the Night differential too. The pattern lab's Night brush goes through `patternCellShiftType`, which resolves to `'base'` when `night.active` is false. Numbers from the real functions (base $65.15, defaults, Night off): sheet preview +$902 gross / +$702 take-home; two such shifts → hero $1,404; the same two nights in a 7-day pattern → lab $1,217 (per shift $781.80 vs $901.80). The sheet is the wrong one: it silently selects a type the nurse turned off, with no chip lit to show why. (If she *deletes* Night instead, `differentials['night']` is undefined and all three surfaces fall back to base — dollars agree, but the sheet still saves an unknown `shiftType` key.) A second instance of the same class of bug was also noted at the dashboard's 'Pick up a weekend night?' card (index.html:3434), which likewise prices `differentials['weekend-eve']` without checking `.active`.
failure: Nurse deactivates Night in Settings ("I only work days"), taps a calendar day, sees no shift-type chip selected but a preview of +$902 gross / +$702 take-home, taps "Add shift". Her calendar and hero now carry a Night-differential shift she cannot see a reason for; the pattern lab, given the same rotation, shows $187 less per paycheck than the hero.
fix: Initialise from the active list: `useState(()=> (Object.entries(differentials).find(([k,d])=>d.active && k!=='overtime')||['base'])[0])`, and add a small effect that resets `shiftType` to that value whenever the current `shiftType` is no longer in `active` (covers a Settings change while the sheet is open). No wage-core function changes; add a harness assertion: deactivate Night, open the sheet, assert a chip is highlighted and the preview equals `shiftGross(base, differentials[thatChip], ...)`.

title: Pattern lab 'Take-home per paycheck' is a multi-paycheck average for cycles that don't divide 14, with no cue — no actual paycheck ever matches it
where: index.html:1282-1298 (patternMetrics span=lcm(n,14), periodGross=gross/periods), labels at 4540 ('Take-home per paycheck'), 4428 ('Take-home / paycheck'), 4447 ('/ paycheck ·')
detail: patternMetrics averages gross over lcm(cycle,14) days and labels the result 'per paycheck'. For 7- and 14-day cycles this equals the hero exactly (verified: pitman, mtw-nights, 3-1-3-7, weekend presets, anchor 3 days off the pay-period start, messy taxes — lab === hero to the cent). For the shipped '4 on, 4 off nights' preset (cycle 8, span 56) and any 28-day or custom cycle, the number is an average of 2-4 different paychecks and the UI never says so. The only drift hint (4534-4536) talks about weekdays, and for a 28-day cycle `drifts` is false so there is no hint at all. Reproduced: 4on4off, base 50, defaults, anchor 2026-09-13, applied 8 weeks: lab says $3,967 take-home / $5,196 gross / 84 hrs; the hero shows $4,457 (96 hrs) for paychecks 1-2 and $3,477 (72 hrs) for paychecks 3-4 — the lab's figure appears on no paycheck. A front-loaded 28-day custom cycle (7 shifts in weeks 1-2, 3 in weeks 3-4): lab $2,838, hero $3,967 then $1,709 — a 40% miss on the first paycheck with `drifts:false` and no warning. Neither surface is mathematically wrong; the lab's label is, because the surface's stated purpose is 'see the paycheck it makes before you commit'. (A parallel repro on the same code path found the shipped 4on4off preset's lab figure of $5,036 falling between $4,212 and $5,677 depending on pay-period offset — same defect, same site.)
failure: Nurse picks the '4 on, 4 off nights' preset, reads 'Take-home per paycheck $3,967', taps 'Put it on the calendar', and the hero for that very period shows $4,457; two paychecks later it shows $3,477. In the side-by-side table she compares 4-on-4-off's $3,967 against Pitman's exact $3,207 as if both were single-paycheck figures.
fix: In PatternLab, when `lcm(metrics.n,14) > 14` (i.e. metrics.n does not divide 14), change the label/sub-line to say it is an average — e.g. 'Take-home per paycheck (avg. over {span/14} paychecks)' at 4540 and a footnote on the 4428/4447 rows — or have patternMetrics also return the per-period min/max (loop the span in 14-day windows, run computeNet on each) and render 'between $3,477 and $4,457, avg $3,967'. Label-only change needs no wage-core session; the min/max variant touches patternMetrics and does.
dissent:
The mechanism the finding grants is not an oversight but a documented design choice made specifically for the case the finding centres on. The comment above patternMetrics (index.html:1253-1256) says: "Money is averaged over lcm(cycle,14) days so a cycle that doesn't divide a fortnight (the 8-day '4 on 4 off') still yields an honest per-paycheck figure." CLAUDE.md's Pattern lab paragraph documents the same: "take-home per paycheck via computeNet() over lcm(cycle,14) days (patternMetrics())". The author looked at the 4-on-4-off preset, saw that its paychecks alternate 96h/72h, and decided the long-run average is the per-paycheck number the lab should show. The finding disagrees with that judgment call; it does not expose a defect.

The lab's framing also makes the average the right metric, not a wrong one. Its money block is a comparison surface: the side-by-side table (4428), the card sub-line (4447), and the "≈ $X a year" line (periodNet*26, 4542) all ask "what does this rotation earn", and for that question a long-run average is the only figure that compares a drifting 8-day cycle against a fixed 14-day Pitman apples-to-apples (Pitman's exact figure is its average too). Rendering "between $3,477 and $4,457" would make the no-nudge side-by-side table harder to read, not more honest. The actual paycheck for a specific period is the hero's job, and the apply flow (confirmApply, 4510) lands the nurse there immediately, where she sees $4,457 for that period before the shifts are worked.

What remains is a copy nit: no "avg." qualifier appears anywhere in the UI (grep for average/avg hits only the code comment), so a nurse could briefly expect the first paycheck to equal the lab figure. That is a one-word label tweak gated on lcm(n,14)>14, not a medium wage-core finding, and the finding's own preferred fix (min/max via computeNet per 14-day window) would open a dedicated Invariant 3 session to solve a labelling question. The front-loaded 28-day custom-cycle repro (40% first-paycheck miss) is a contrived pattern, and the hero corrects it the moment it is applied.
